----------------


This examination is being given to fill 1 vacancy in the Behavioral Health Services department and to establish an eligible list to fill future vacancies. jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Musicians at Play Foundation, Inc.

Seeks full time, hybrid **Director of Development**

**WHO WE ARE**: Musicians at Play Foundation is a Los Angeles–based nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high\-quality music education, mentorship, and career pathways for young musicians from underserved communities. Beginning in kindergarten and continuing through college, its instrumental music programs create a clear, guided journey that leads students into paid professional positions in the music industry. Through initiatives such as the RISE Film Scoring Orchestra, the Civic Orchestra of Los Angeles, conducting academies, and pre\-apprenticeship training, participants gain hands\-on experience alongside industry professionals in real\-world studio and performance settings while developing artistry, discipline, and career readiness.

**Director of Development** 

We are seeking to grow our team with a new hire, Director of Development. The Director will lead Musicians at Play (MAP) fundraising strategy, donor cultivation, and revenue generation to support its mission. The candidate will create comprehensive fundraising plans, develop and manage donor relationships, oversee special events, and lead a development team. This role requires expertise in donor cultivation, grant writing, and strategic planning.

This role is a hybrid one and requires familiarity with the Los Angeles area arts \& culture sector as well as in\-person presence at a variety of meetings and events.

The current development team consists of a Grant Writer, Finance Manager, Events/Sponsorship Coordinator, and Website, Database \& Communications Manager. Development Director will report to the Executive Director and Board of Directors.

**Core Responsibilities**

* **Fundraising Strategy:** Develop and execute an annual fundraising strategy to meet financial goals, including donor cultivation and retention.
* **Donor Management:** Build and maintain relationships with major donors, corporations, and stakeholders.
* **Development Team Leadership**

Provide leadership and collaboration to the development staff. Work in partnership with the Board of Directors and the Executive Director on fundraising initiatives \& strategy.

* **Revenue Diversification:** Identify and pursue new funding opportunities, including grants and sponsorships.
* **Events and Communications:** Oversee the planning of fundraising events and the creation of marketing materials for campaigns.
* **Reporting and Compliance:** Track donor data, manage the development budget, and report progress to the Executive Director and Board.
* at public events and in other contexts as needed. Be a willing partner with other staff in all aspects of MAP’s mission.
* MAP’s funding base to increase unrestricted and restricted funds from all constituencies and launch appropriate programs and initiatives.
* through active communication and delegation
* for fund\-raising and cultivation of donors and volunteers through major and planned giving, annual giving, corporate and foundation relations, special events, membership and community relations in addition to prospect research and donor stewardship. Coordinate all fund development activities including but not limited to:

Strengthen relationships with current donors and conduct major Donor Cultivation Work with staff and Board to increase contributions at the $5000 \- $100,000 level. Increase the gifts of current donors and overall number of donors; coordinate prospect research.

* staff, board, and outside consultants to help identify and recruit sponsors for MAP’s programs and initiatives.
* with Executive Director and Board to strengthen relations with the corporate community.
* with appropriate staff on all public outreach efforts, including the development of public outreach materials such as print and electronic newsletters, direct mail, press releases, brochures, social media and website to promote MAP’s message.
* Executive Director and Board to integrate a planned giving program with annual fund donor cultivation and solicitation efforts.
* staff, Board, and volunteers to help MAP successfully produce yearly fundraising events.
* reports evaluating the fundraising efforts and progress. Create an annual report of accomplishments and future goals.

**Key Qualifications**

* **Experience:** 5\+ years of experience in professional fundraising, donor relations, and non\-profit development.
* **Skills:** Strong written/oral communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
* **Attributes:** Entrepreneurial spirit, passion for the organization's mission, and proficiency in areas described (above).
* **Familiarity with** the entertainment and arts \& culture LA landscape, especially as it pertains to building our donor base.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

We are looking for a Senior MLOps engineer to work closely with Data Scientists to build and deploy ML models on a modern MLOps stack.
As an Executive Director Machine Learning Engineer on the Recommendation Engine team, you'll implement fine\-tuning and reinforcement learning algorithms on large compute clusters, build and run real\-time and batch model serving systems, hyper\-parameter tuning at scale, model monitoring, production validation and other activities vital for model development, testing and deployment in a well\-managed, controlled environment.
Our product, Personalization and Insights, builds and supports high throughput, low latency applications which leverage state of the art machine learning architectures, and which are deployed in AWS. These applications power personalized experiences across Chase Consumer \& Community Banking channels, to help weave a user experience that includes traditional banking services with other services in the Travel, Merchant Offer Shopping, and Dining spaces.
Job responsibilities
* Build, deploy, and maintain robust pipelines for distributed training on GPU\-enabled clusters to support scalable machine learning workflows.
* Develop and manage high\-volume real\-time and batch inference systems, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.
* Implement quantization techniques and deploy open\-weight large language models (LLMs) on modern serving stacks such as vLLM on Ray to maximize efficiency and resource utilization.
* Oversee the management and optimization of vector databases to support advanced AI and machine learning applications.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive monitoring and observability pipelines to ensure system health, performance, and rapid issue resolution.
* Collaborate with cross\-functional teams to integrate new technologies and continuously improve existing infrastructure.
* Partner with product, architecture, and other engineering teams to define scalable and performant technical solutions.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
* BS in Computer Science or related Engineering field with 10\+ years of experience Or MS degree in Computer Science or related Engineering field with 6\+ years experience.
* Solid knowledge and extensive experience in Python or in cloud computing and AWS.
* Understanding of quantization techniques such as PTQ, AWQ etc. used to quantize LLMs for accelerating inference on specific GPU architectures
* Solid understanding of Transformer models and challenges involved in serving large transformer\-based models
* Solid understanding of ML training, especially latest reinforcement learning algorithms such as GRPO and DAPO
* Experience in systems engineering fundamentals: caching, CUDA, autoscaling, high throughput, low latency, x\-region resilient applications
* Deep knowledge and passion for data science fundamentals, training and deploying models
* Experience in monitoring and observability tools to monitor model input/output and features stats
* Solid grounding in engineering fundamentals and analytical mindset

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills
* Experience with recommendation and personalization systems is a plus.
* CUDA experience is a big plus
* Solid fundamentals and experience in containers (docker ecosystem), container orchestration systems \[Kubernetes, ECS]
* Experience with Ray, vLLM, RL libraries such as verl/trl
* Good knowledge of Databases

**Position Overview**

**Job Title:** Chief Operating Officer (COO)

**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer (CEO) / President of the Board

**Locations:** Ontario, California and Mishawaka, Indiana

**Classification:** Full\-Time, Exempt

**Travel Required:** Regular travel between both plant locations (approximately 20\-40%)

This is a hands\-on, 5 days a week in person working COO role designed for an experienced operations leader who thrives in a small manufacturing environment. The COO will be actively involved in day\-to\-day plant operations while providing operational and strategic leadership to drive efficiency, quality, and growth across both California and Indiana facilities. This is not a behind\-the\-desk position; the right candidate rolls up their sleeves and works alongside the team. To carry out these responsibilities effectively, the COO must be present at one of the facilities each day.

**Company Overview**

We are a small manufacturing company with production facilities in Ontario, California and Mishawaka, Indiana. Our operations are built on quality craftsmanship and a team\-first culture. jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Executive Director provides leadership for Faith and Grace, Inc, (FnG) by centering the organization’s mission while effectively implementing programs, supervising staff, exercising sound fiscal oversight, and building strong community partnerships. This role is responsible for day\-to\-day operations and long\-term sustainability. This is a full‑time (40 hours), exempt leadership position that reports directly to the Board of Directors

Executive Director Responsibilities

* Provide community and agency leadership to ensure FnG’s mission is effectively implemented across all programs and initiatives.
* Ensure fiscal accountability in collaboration with the agency’s bookkeeper, Treasurer, and Board of Directors, including budget development and monitoring, grant reporting, and administration of donor and grant funds.
* Develop and execute strategic plans together with the Board, staff, and community partners focusing on FnG’s mission, goals, and sustainability.
* Oversee daily operations and program delivery, including community education and outreach, shelter and hotline services, case management, and other survivor support programs.
* Cultivate a trauma\-informed, inclusive, and equitable workplace culture that promotes the provision of trauma\-informed services for survivors, staff well\-being, and retention of skilled staff.
* Manage the Recruitment, training, supervision, and mentorship of staff and volunteers to provide high\-quality services to survivors and the community.
* Uphold best practices in trauma\-informed service delivery for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and other forms of intimate violence.
* Maintain confidentiality across settings, including employment records, client services, and organizational matters.
* Strengthen and expand partnerships with community organizations, funders, government, and law enforcement to coordinate services for the benefit of survivors.
* Lead fundraising and development efforts with the Board of Directors, including donor cultivation, grant development, and major events to secure and diversify revenue.
* Develop and maintain organizational performance metrics to inform data\-driven decision\-making by the Board in all areas of agency functions, with an emphasis on making cost\-effective decisions regarding the provision of program services and fundraising that align with the agency’s mission.
* Manage complex organizational projects and systems improvements, ensuring effective planning, resource allocation, and timely project completion.
* Serve as the public leader for FnG and its mission by building community relationships and advocating for the agency and its mission in public settings.
* Promote policies and programs that ensure strong succession planning, leadership development, organizational stability, and the long\-term provision of mission\-focused services and programs.

Required Qualifications

* Arizona DPS Level One Fingerprint Clearance Card
* The Executive Director must uphold the highest standards of confidentiality in accordance with federal and state laws, including VAWA, FVPSA, VOCA and HIPAA‑related provisions where applicable. This role requires strict protection of all survivor information, organizational records, and sensitive operational data. The Executive Director will ensure that no personally identifiable information (PII), case details, or client‑related communications are disclosed without legally permissible authorization.
* Professional experience working with survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and other forms of intimate violence or another closely related human services area.
* Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, make difficult and time\-sensitive decisions, provide services to marginalized and vulnerable communities, and engage in conflict resolution across settings.
* Minimum of five years of nonprofit management or executive leadership experience or three years with a relevant master’s degree.
* Proven success in donor development and fundraising, including grant writing, major gifts solicitation and relationship management.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking and advocacy experience.
* Proven ability to ensure compliance with nonprofit governance, financial, and legal requirements
* Extensive knowledge and demonstrated ability to develop and implement annual budgets, engage in fiscal forecasting, read and draft financial reports, and properly administer donor, grant, and public funds accurately and appropriately.
* Demonstrated ability to work in collaboration with Board of Directors and fiscal managers to maintain the fiscal health of the organization.

Preferred Qualifications

* Master’s degree or equivalent experience.
* Experience supervising direct service teams and implementing trauma\-informed practices.
* Experience managing capital campaigns or major development projects.
* Prior experience serving as Executive Director or senior leader in a non\-profit organization.

Work Environment

Work is primarily performed in a standard, climate\-controlled office setting. The position requires extended periods of computer work and frequent interaction with staff, clients, and community members. Some evening and weekend work is required to attend events or respond to organizational needs. The role involves occasional lifting (up to 50 lbs.) and travel throughout the community.

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $95,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, AEROSPACE HERITAGE FOUNDATION OF UTAH
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Heritage Foundation of Utah (AHFU) is a non\-profit organization with a primary mission to provide financial support for the Hill Aerospace Museum in Roy, Utah. The Foundation is seeking an experienced Executive Director who is passionate about our mission and able to lead our organization with vision and excellence.

The Executive Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of the Foundation’s operations, including fundraising, program development, financial management, marketing, strategic planning and staff supervision. The Executive Director will report to the Chairman of the AHFU and will work closely with the AHFU Board of Directors to promote and implement its funding priorities.

In addition to their operational responsibilities, the Executive Director must be a passionate leader who inspires others to engage with our mission. He or she works directly with the Board of Directors, the Foundation staff, the Air Force Museum Director, and his staff to ensure that the organization is fulfilling its mission and serving its constituents effectively. The Executive Director will also be responsible for cultivating and maintaining relationships with key stakeholders, including, donors, partners, and community leaders.

Our Executive Director will be a motivational leader with a proven track record of success in nonprofit management, passionate about the Hill Aerospace Museum, and committed to achieving our goals. The Executive Director must be a strategic thinker who is able to balance short\-term needs with long\-term planning. He or she will have excellent communication skills and be able to represent the Foundation to a variety of audiences.

Collaborate with the Board of Directors to ensure the organization is fulfilling its mission

Provide regular updates to the Board regarding the organization’s operations and performance

Work with the Board to develop and implement policies and procedures which support the Foundation’s missions and goals

Provide training to new Board members to familiarize them with Foundation policies and procedures

**STAFF MANAGEMENT AND LEADERSHIP:**

Serve as a servant leader to the Foundation staff providing guidance, motivation, and support in their duties

Foster a positive work environment promoting teamwork, collaboration and staff growth

Provide regular feedback to staff members, both in the form of ongoing coaching and formal evaluations, to ensure they are meeting performance expectations and helping them to grow in their roles

Model and promote the organization’s values and culture, setting a high standard for ethical and effective behavior

**FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT:**

Oversee the organization’s financial management, ensuring that the organization is financially sound and operating with financial prudence for long term sustainability

Develop and oversee the organization’s annual budget, working with the Financial Committee and the Museum Director to ensure that it aligns with the organization’s goals and priorities

Monitor financial performance on an ongoing basis with the Foundation Treasurer and Bookkeeper to ensure the organization is operating within its budget

Ensure that financial reports are accurate and provided to the Board in a timely manner, including working with the external auditor on the annual Foundation audit

FUNDRAISING AND DEVELOPMENT:

Develop and lead the implementation of a comprehensive fundraising and development strategy that aligns with the Foundation’s mission and goals, including targets for both restricted and unrestricted donations

Work with the Board of Directors and the Air Force Museum Director to establish fundraising priorities and opportunities, to include annual giving campaigns, special events, and grant applications

Provide leadership and direction to staff and volunteers involved in fundraising and development activities, ensuring all efforts are aligned with the organization’s goals and priorities

Develop and implement donor stewardship plans to maintain strong relationships with donors, including regular communication, recognition, and engagement opportunities

PROGRAM DEVELOP AND MANAGEMENT:

Develop and implement a strategic program planning process to identify programs that align with the organization’s mission and goals

Work with the Air Force Museum Director and staff to ensure Foundation programs are consistent with the Director’s programs, and where possible, complement those programs for the betterment of the Museum

Where possible, assist the Museum Director and his staff in establishing exceptional education programs, both in\-house and outreach, which are an important part of the Museum’s mission

MARKETING, COMMUNICATION AND PUBLIC SPEAKING:

Continue the development of a comprehensive marketing and communications strategy to increase the Foundation’s visibility and reach

Act as the organization’s spokesperson and represent the Foundation at public events and speaking engagements

Work with the Air Force Museum Director and the Board of Directors to establish and implement an effective marketing strategy for the Museum

STRATEGIC PLANNING:

Work with the Board of Directors to develop and implement the Foundation’s strategic plan

Identify opportunities for growth and expansion and plans to pursue them, adjusting the strategic plan accordingly

Ensure the organization’s programs and activities align with the strategic plan and the Air Force Museum Director’s strategic plan for the Museum

jobs.title: Development Director - Immigrant Support Services
jobs.description:
**The Berkshire Immigrant Center (BIC) is seeking a Development Director** to join our leadership team and oversee all fundraising efforts. This role combines strategic planning with hands\-on execution and offers the opportunity to make a meaningful, community\-facing impact in support of BIC’s mission.

As immigration processes grow more complex, fundraising helps BIC sustain and expand access to immigration legal services, keep the community informed, and adapt programs as needs evolve. Philanthropy keeps client costs low, supports free citizenship preparation classes, and increases emergency assistance for basic needs such as rent, utilities, and application fees. It also strengthens BIC’s long\-term sustainability by expanding our immigration legal capacity, deepening statewide connections, and building the resources that uniquely position us to serve immigrant families across the region.

Fundraising at BIC is a shared effort. The Executive Director (ED) is actively involved in major donor strategy, solicitations, and grant development, while the Board supports cultivation and outreach. The Development Director reports directly to the ED and is supported by a part\-time Development Assistant.

We are seeking a highly organized, detail\-oriented professional who excels at building meaningful relationships with donors, volunteers, and committees. **BIC seeks to raise over $1,000,000 this fiscal year**, primarily through private donations from individuals, companies, and foundations.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Partner with the Board of Trustees, ED, and Development and Benefit Committees to design and implement a comprehensive development program that increases annual revenue.
* In alignment with the Strategic Plan, help develop and implement a long\-term fundraising strategy with the ED and external consultant.
* Meet regularly with the ED to review progress toward goals, monitor revenue, and adjust priorities as needed.
* Lead execution of the Annual Appeal and a signature spring fundraising event
* Manage donor database operations (Little Green Light), including gift processing, acknowledgments, reporting, and mailing lists.
* Cultivate and steward donors while managing a portfolio of prospects and supporters
* Research prospective funders; write and submit grant proposals and reports; and maintain strong relationships with foundation and institutional funders.
* Support communications and campaign messaging across email, social media, and other channels.
* Serve as an ambassador for BIC in the community, building relationships with individuals, foundations, businesses, and community partners.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
* 3\-5 years of nonprofit development experience with demonstrated fundraising execution.
* Proven success securing grants and individual gifts in the four\- and five\-figure range
* Experience planning and executing an Annual Appeal and one signature fundraising event.
* Strong writing and editing skills for proposals, appeals, and donor communications.
* Proficiency with Little Green Light or other constituency management system.
* Strong project management skills, ability to prioritize and manage multiple deadlines.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the ED, Board, and volunteers.
* Commitment to ethical, non\-extractive storytelling, client confidentiality, and cultural humility in an immigrant\-serving context.
* Familiarity with local and regional funders is a plus.
* Multilingual skills, particularly Spanish, are a plus.
* Strong project management and organizational skills, ability to prioritize and manage multiple deadlines.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the Executive Director, Board, and volunteers.
* Commitment to ethical, non\-extractive storytelling, client confidentiality, and cultural humility in an immigrant\-serving context.
* Familiarity with Berkshire County and Massachusetts funders and community networks is a plus.
* Multilingual skills, particularly Spanish, are a plus.

**To Apply**

Interested candidates can either submit a cover letter or choose to answer any of the following questions:

* How do you approach donor and grant storytelling for immigrant\-serving work in a way that is accurate, dignified, and non\-extractive? Share a brief example.

jobs.title: Interim Executive Director, ULI Kansas City
jobs.description:
The Urban Land Institute is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit research and education organization supported by its members. Founded in 1936, the Institute has more than 48,000 members worldwide representing the full spectrum of land use and real estate development disciplines across private enterprise and public service. ULI’s mission is to shape the future of the built environment for transformative impact in communities worldwide.

**About ULI Kansas City**


ULI Kansas City is the Institute’s home in one of the Midwest’s most dynamic real estate markets, connecting developers, investors, designers, public officials, and civic leaders around the region’s biggest land use questions. Through signature programs like the quarterly Envision series, Technical Assistance Panels, and member\-led committees spanning Young Leaders, Emerging Developers, and REDI, the council shapes how Kansas City grows.


The council is entering a defining new chapter. In early 2027, the ULI Nebraska satellite will transition into an independent Local Organizing Committee, and ULI Kansas City will move forward as a focused, city\-anchored district council. That change creates a rare leadership moment: the chance to rebuild the council’s committee structure, re\-energize its membership, and set the direction for what ULI Kansas City becomes next.

**The Role**


This is a leadership role built around relationships and ownership. Reporting to the Senior Director, District Councils, and working in close partnership with the District Council Chair and a highly engaged member leadership, the Interim Executive Director owns the council’s program of work end to end: strategy, programming, membership, sponsorship, communications, and operations.


The mandate is clear: guide the council smoothly through the Nebraska transition, grow membership and revenue in the Kansas City market, and build the platform for the council’s next stage. The leader in this seat will directly shape ULI Kansas City’s long\-term structure and direction.


This is a full\-time, benefits\-eligible interim appointment of approximately 12 months. Based on the council’s performance through the transition, including membership and revenue growth, ULI may consider establishing a permanent Executive Director role at the end of the term. This appointment is interim, and conversion or continued employment beyond the term is not guaranteed.

**What You Will Do**

**Transition \& Growth Leadership**

* Lead ULI Kansas City through the transition of the ULI Nebraska satellite to an independent Local Organizing Committee, managing member communications, programming continuity, and financial planning through the change.
* Develop and execute a membership growth and retention plan for the Kansas City market, rebuilding the council’s committee structure and volunteer engagement model.
* Grow sponsorship, grant, and program revenue against defined revenue and membership targets.
* Establish ULI Kansas City’s identity and program of work as a standalone, city\-focused district council.

**Council Leadership \& Operations**

* Develop and implement a strategic program of work, budget, and staffing plan with clearly defined outcomes and methods to measure success.
* Oversee all district council committees, including Management, Programs, Membership Engagement, Young Leaders, Emerging Developers, REDI, TAPs (Technical Assistance Panels), and Sponsorship; engage existing volunteers and create new opportunities for active member involvement.
* Support the Chair, Advisory, Management, Governance, and other leadership committees, building out administration, leadership development, and succession planning.
* Oversee programs, communications, social media, and reporting, including the quarterly Envision program series.
* Develop and manage event and committee budgets, including forecasting, tracking, and reconciliation.

**Relationships \& Sponsorship**

* Build strong relationships within the Kansas City community and with ULI Americas/Global and other district councils.
* Work directly with ULI members, including Advisory Board and Management Committee members, member firms, sponsors, prospects, vendors, partner organizations, and consultants.
* Build funding relationships and strategic partnerships with existing sponsors, expand the sponsor network, and pursue and manage grant applications.

**Staff Leadership**

* Direct and develop ULI Kansas City’s part\-time contractor

**What are we looking for?**

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree required, and/or 5\+ years of related nonprofit or membership organization experience.
* Demonstrated ability to grow and retain membership and generate revenue through sponsorship, grants, and programs.
* Ability to plan and oversee high\-quality events, and to work effectively with diverse groups of people, including members, corporate leaders, politicians, educators, public officials, and ULI national staff.
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple concurrent workstreams with responsible follow\-through.
* Strong oral and written communication skills, and strong organizational and time management skills.

**Preferred**

jobs.title: VP, Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**If you are qualified and interested, please apply here (https://thinkingahead.com/opportunities/job/e8652474\-a0a9\-46f7\-9f0f\-f2de0804219a/) with your resume and cover letter. Do not apply via the Tennessee Aquarium careers site.**



The Tennessee Aquarium is seeking an accomplished, strategic, and highly collaborative Chief Operating Officer to help lead one of the nation’s most respected aquariums through an ambitious new era of growth and impact.



Located on the banks of the Tennessee River in downtown Chattanooga, the Tennessee Aquarium is a nationally recognized leader in freshwater conservation, education, research, and exceptional guest experiences. Since opening in 1992, the Aquarium has welcomed millions of visitors, helped catalyze Chattanooga’s celebrated riverfront renaissance, and built an extraordinary reputation for connecting people with nature and protecting the remarkable freshwater biodiversity of the Southeast.



Today, the Aquarium is building on that strong foundation while intentionally shifting its focus from business maintenance to impact growth. A new strategic platform is nearing completion, a ten\-year facilities master planning process is on the horizon, and significant investments are underway in veterinary medicine, conservation science, education, guest experiences, and organizational capacity. In 2025, the Aquarium welcomed more than 784,000 guests while continuing to achieve strong financial, conservation, and educational results.


**The Opportunity**



Reporting to President \& CEO Andy Wood, the Chief Operating Officer will serve as a key strategic and operating partner, helping translate the Aquarium’s ambitious vision into coordinated action.



This is much more than a traditional operations role. The COO will oversee a broad portfolio of functions while helping ensure that the people, systems, facilities, resources, and organizational capacity are in place to support the Aquarium’s next phase of growth. The role will influence guest experience and earned revenue; facilities and major capital projects; leadership development and organizational culture; safety, risk, and business continuity; long\-term exhibit and facilities planning; and implementation of the Aquarium’s emerging strategic plan.



The successful candidate will also play an important role in strengthening collaboration and accountability across a highly specialized organization and developing the next generation of Aquarium leaders. This individual will serve as a trusted partner to a visionary, energetic CEO — bringing sound judgment, prioritization, candid counsel, disciplined execution, and the ability to turn ambitious ideas into measurable results.


**Key Responsibilities**



The Chief Operating Officer will:


* Translate strategic vision into clear priorities, operating plans, and measurable results.
* Lead guest\-facing operations with a strong focus on hospitality, attendance, earned revenue growth, and exceptional guest experiences.
* Provide executive leadership for facilities, infrastructure, major capital projects, operational safety, disaster preparedness, and business continuity.
* Partner in the development of the Aquarium’s ten\-year facilities master plan and long\-term exhibit priorities.
* Develop leaders, strengthen management capabilities, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, hospitality, and shared purpose.
* Help lead the organization thoughtfully through growth and change while preserving the strengths of an already successful institution.
* Strengthen cross\-functional coordination and help highly specialized teams operate around shared organizational priorities.
* Serve as a respected representative of the Tennessee Aquarium within the Association of Zoos \& Aquariums and the broader professional community.


**The Successful Candidate**



Strong candidates will bring:


* Seven or more years of senior leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading complex, multi\-functional operations and senior\-level teams.
* Experience in an executive leadership position with a cultural institution is strongly preferred.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, P\&L responsibility, revenue generation, resource allocation, and expense management.
* A record of translating strategy and vision into disciplined execution.
* Exceptional judgment and the confidence to serve as a genuine operating partner to a CEO.
* High emotional intelligence and demonstrated success developing leaders, building trust, and navigating different personalities and perspectives.
* Experience guiding organizations and teams through meaningful growth and change.
* Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively with a Board, executive colleagues, employees at all levels, and external stakeholders.
* A genuine commitment to the Aquarium’s mission and an understanding of how operational excellence, guest experience, revenue, conservation, and education work together to advance impact.


A bachelor’s degree is required; an advanced degree is preferred.


**Why Chattanooga?**



Chattanooga combines an exceptional quality of life with an increasingly dynamic economy. Surrounded by mountains and the Tennessee River, the city offers extraordinary access to outdoor recreation alongside a vibrant downtown, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, family activities, and comparatively affordable living. Chattanooga became the first National Park City in North America in 2025 and is continuing to invest in major new downtown and riverfront development.

**The Organization:** The Georgia Historical Society (GHS) is the premier independent statewide institution responsible for collecting, examining, and teaching Georgia history. GHS houses the oldest and most distinguished collection of materials related exclusively to Georgia history in the nation. To learn more, go to www.georgiahistory.com
  
  

**Job Summary:** The Director of Development is responsible for supporting the GHS mission and vision through acquisition of funding necessary to expand and sustain GHS programs. This person will maintain a high level of understanding of the GHS model and exhibit passion for the GHS mission and oversee development and implementation of annual and campaign\-specific fundraising plans designed to obtain philanthropic gifts to advance the GHS research and educational mission. The Director of Development supports the efforts of the President/CEO, the Vice President/COO, the Board of Curators, key volunteers, and others to raise funds to meet specific measurable fundraising goals and monitor progress against those goals. Responsibilities will include creating and maintaining records and reports of development\-related activities (e.g., campaign reports, donor reports). This role is responsible for formulating and supporting a funding strategy and for executing and/or overseeing the implementation of a development plan which deepens the commitment of existing donors, increases the number of overall supporters, and creates opportunities for all to contribute to GHS’s mission in practical and meaningful ways. The successful candidate will be energized by the opportunity to strengthen the existing development program and enhance the fundraising results of GHS. GHS boasts an influential, dynamic Board of Curators comprised of leaders from across the state of Georgia; the board is actively engaged in development efforts.
  
  

This is a full\-time, benefited, position located in Savannah, GA.
  
  

Job Duties and Responsibilities (incumbent may perform other duties as assigned)
  
  

Development (Prospect Identification, Research, Relationship Management, and Solicitation) Percentage of Role – 40%
  
  

Works with CEO and COO to develop, oversee, and implement a comprehensive annual fundraising plan inclusive of board, corporate, foundation, individual donor, and membership giving as well as development events. Oversees annual and ongoing campaigns, to include the Annual Appeal, Georgia History Festival, Endowment, and Planned Giving campaigns. This includes working with others to coordinate efforts of the CEO, COO, board members, and volunteers to solicit donations by researching, analyzing, and identifying major corporate, foundation, and individual donors, and assists with developing solicitation proposals and talking points for the CEO, board members, and other leadership as needed. Works with the senior leadership team to identify funds needed and preferred funding targets and approaches. Identifies and cultivates major gift prospects, as well as corporate and foundation donors. Stewards relationships with existing donors implementing follow\-up communication and expressing gratitude frequently and in a timely manner. Efforts are focused on advanced relationship building primarily over the phone to support institutional development plans and initiatives that support the CEO’s relationship building and development activities. Working with others, creates proposals for corporations and grant making foundations and directs the necessary follow\-up reports for funders related to all grant awards received. Drafts grant applications in a timely manner and maintains follow\-up communication with foundation representatives. Works closely with PR/Communications to develop and execute effective donor communications and marketing materials including preparation of all fundraising appeals and materials, including targeted email, direct mail, and social media campaigns.
  
  

Campaign Strategies and Recordkeeping (Development Strategies, Data Management, and Reporting) Percentage of Role – 25%

jobs.description:
The **VNAHospice of the Southwest Region** of Rutland is looking for a full time **Director of Philanthropy**. Would you like to work for a caring and supportive home health and hospice agency that values its employees? If so, please read on!

**ABOUT VNAHOSPICE OF THE SOUTHWEST REGION**


Based in Vermont, we are one of the largest non\-profit home health and hospice care agency that delivers a wide range of advanced medical care with compassion, dependability, and expertise to people of all ages. Our mission is to provide the best care for every person and to put a little more heart and soul into healthcare along the way. We strive to give customized care to individuals with chronic diseases and conditions as well as those who need short\-term care. For our services, we have been recognized as one of the nation's top 100 performing home health agencies by HomeCare Elite.

**A DAY IN THE LIFE OF THE DIRECTOR OF PHILANTHROPY:**


This position leads the Agency's comprehensive fundraising program to increase charitable support and advance its mission and strategic priorities. This position builds relationships with donors and community partners, oversees philanthropy staff and programs, and collaborates with leadership, Board members, and colleagues across the Agency to achieve fundraising goals. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

* Provides strategic direction and oversight for the Agency's comprehensive philanthropy program, including annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, grants, sponsorships, special campaigns, events, municipal funding, and other charitable revenue opportunities.
* Develop and implement an annual philanthropy plan aligned with the Agency's mission, strategic priorities, and financial goals.
* Establishes annual fundraising goals and develops and manages the department budget in collaboration with the CEO and CFO as well as other leadership as appropriate.
* Maintains a personal portfolio of donors and prospects and participates in all aspects of the donor cycle, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, recognition, and stewardship.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, prospective donors, businesses, foundations, community partners, and other stakeholders to expand philanthropic support.
* Identifies and develops opportunities for planned gifts and special, capital, or endowment campaigns that advance the Agency's long\-term strategic priorities.
* Provides oversight of the Agency's grant program, including identifying funding opportunities, coordinating applications, monitoring deadlines and deliverables, and supporting required reporting and compliance.
* Leads the planning and execution of annual appeals, fundraising events, donor\-recognition activities, sponsorships, and approved third\-party fundraising initiatives. Maintains a coordinated calendar of philanthropy activities and deadlines.
* Oversee the preparation of donor communications, solicitation and sponsorship materials, acknowledgments, impact reports, and stewardship communications in collaboration with Marketing and Communications, as appropriate.
* Supervises, supports, and evaluates the Philanthropy Database Coordinator and other assigned staff, providing clear expectations, training, feedback, and professional development. Oversee the accuracy and integrity of the donor database and the effective coordination of municipal and town funding requests, mailings, records, reporting, and follow\-up activities.
* Oversee the Agency's thrift store as a mission\-based fundraising and community engagement program, including supervision of thrift store employees, support and recognition of volunteers, monitoring of financial performance, and collaboration with Marketing and Communications on promotions and events.
* Serves as the primary staff liaison to the Board Development Committee, supporting the committee chair, preparing reports and meeting materials, coordinating follow\-up, and engaging committee members in philanthropy activities.
* Represents the Agency at donor visits, community meetings, events, presentations, and other activities; maintains donor confidentiality; follows ethical fundraising practices; participates in Agency\-wide initiatives; and performs other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Five to seven years of relevant experience in community relations, planned giving, major donor solicitation, and event planning required in a nonprofit, education, or public service environment required.
* Demonstrated success in managing a donor portfolio, with a track record of increasing revenue through effective cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.
* Experience supporting and managing up to senior leaders, volunteer leaders/board members, and high\-level volunteers.
* Valid State driver's license required. Ability to successfully pass pre\-employment adult, child and VCIC background checks required.

**VNAHSR benefits for full\-time employees include:**


Generous paid time off, group health, dental, vision, life, STD and LTD insurance, 401K with 4% match, and more.  

Continuing education tuition assistance for work\-related courses, to eligible staff

jobs.description:
**ABOUT THE MUHAMMAD ALI CENTER** 

The Muhammad Ali Center was created to honor the life of “The Greatest”. Based in Louisville, KY, the Center is a multicultural organization, an award\-winning museum, and a global beacon for social justice. We exist to mobilize Ali’s legacy to foster respect, inspire generations of changemakers, and advance social justice, creating a world where all people can achieve their own greatness.

From the Ali Center's inception, Diversity, Equity, \& Inclusion have been central to our core values. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes diverse viewpoints are critical to our global impact, and we actively foster a culture where inclusion is everyone’s responsibility.

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**

The President \& Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide the visionary leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight required to champion the Ali Center’s mission and drive its next phase of global growth. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CEO holds full executive authority and accountability for all Center operations, including a $5M operating budget, a dedicated team of 30\+ staff and volunteers, programming and the operations of our world\-class facility.

As a primary public face of the Center, the CEO will convert mission into measurable global results. A proven track record of high\-level fundraising is paramount; the CEO will spearhead philanthropic growth across individual, corporate, foundational, and government sectors to ensure long\-term financial sustainability.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES** 

**Strategic Leadership \& Brand Advocacy** 

· **Drive Vision \& Growth**: Lead the execution of the strategic plan, aligning operational goals, revenue development, and programming with the Center’s core values.

· **Global Vision \& Expansion**: Drive the strategy to elevate the Center’s national and international profile. Collaborate closely with the senior leadership team to strategically cultivate relationships with major donors, community leaders, and global partners, positioning the Center for broad geographic and philanthropic growth.

**Revenue Generation \& Sustainability** 

· **Capital Cultivation**: Personally initiate and lead major fundraising campaigns, with a proven ability to close gifts at the 6\-figure (required) and 7\-figure (preferred) levels.

· **Diversify Revenue**: Expand funding streams through corporate partnerships, licensing, institutional grants, and strategic monetization of the Center’s assets.

**Operational Excellence \& Culture**

· **People \& Culture**: Inspire, mentor, and retain a high\-performing, diverse team, fostering a collaborative, respectful, and mission\-driven workplace culture.

· **Impact Measurement**: Establish rigorous evaluation frameworks to assess programming efficacy, ensuring initiatives remain impactful, sustainable, and tied to the mission.

· **Board Partnership**: Maintain transparent, regular, and strategic communications with the Board of Directors to optimize governance and organizational health.

**PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE \& QUALIFICATIONS** 

The ideal candidate is a visionary, energetic, and collaborative leader who pair executive acumen with the empathy, kindness, and welcoming spirit modeled by Muhammad Ali.

**REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:**

· **Executive Leadership**: A minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in high\-profile nonprofits, NGOs, educational institutions, foundations, or corporate entities.

· **Fundraising Excellence**: A documented history of securing major gifts and scaling philanthropic revenue from diverse donor networks.

· **Business \& Fiscal Acumen**: Proven experience managing multi\-million dollar budgets, with a strong sensitivity to expense management and a track record of driving balance financial performance.

· **Partnership \& Alliance Building**: Skilled at building consensus among diverse stakeholders, including board members, elected officials, community leaders, and international partners.

· **Governance**: Proven success collaborating with and leveraging a highly engaged Board of Directors.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:** 

* This role operates within a multi\-level facility and requires the ability to navigate the space and assist with exhibit and display setup as needed. The Muhammad Ali Center is ADA compliant and provides reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable laws.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
**About the Role**

Kids’ Meals is seeking an accomplished, mission\-driven Senior Director of Advancement to provide strategic fundraising for the organization, from annual, mid\-level, major, recurring, and planned giving donors.

This position develops and executes strategies to acquire, cultivate, solicit, steward, and increase giving from individual and foundation donors while building a sustainable pipeline that supports Kids’ Meals’ long\-term revenue goals.

Reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, the Senior Director partners closely with the Executive Leadership, Board of Directors, and Development and Communications teams to increase philanthropic revenue, enhance donor relationships, and create meaningful donor experiences connected to the mission of ending childhood hunger.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Donor Strategy:** Develop and execute a comprehensive strategy to grow annual, mid\-level, major, recurring, and planned giving revenue.
* **Revenue Performance:** Establish and achieve revenue, donor acquisition, retention, , and pipeline development goals in partnership with the Chief Advancement Officer.
* **Portfolio Management:** Build and manage a portfolio of approximately 100 prospects capable of making gifts of $5,000 or more.
* **Major Gift Fundraising:** Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward donors and prospects, with an emphasis on securing five\- and six\-figure gifts.
* **Moves Management:** Design and implement processes and tracking systems that support consistent donor identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* **Executive Partnership:** Partner with the Chief Advancement Officer and CEO on the cultivation and solicitation of board members, community leaders, high\-capacity prospects, and other priority donors.
* **Annual and Recurring Giving:** Oversee annual giving campaigns, giving circles, recurring donor programs, and other opportunities to increase donor engagement and long\-term support.
* **Planned Giving:** Develop and grow the organization’s planned giving program through prospect identification, donor education, cultivation, recognition, and stewardship.
* **Donor Stewardship:** Develop and oversee stewardship efforts that recognizes, engages, and retains donors at all giving levels.
* **Donor Communications:** Collaborate with the Communications team to create donor\-centered appeals, impact stories, campaign materials, and stewardship communications.
* **Donor Engagement:** Partner with the Special Events and Volunteer Experience teams to create meaningful mission\-focused experiences for donors.
* **Data and Reporting:** Use donor and giving data to identify trends, segment audiences, evaluate performance, and uncover opportunities for donor acquisition and increased giving.
* **Financial Collaboration:** Partner with Finance and Development Operations to support accurate gift processing, reconciliation, revenue tracking, budgeting, and forecasting.
* **Leadership Reporting:** Prepare reports and dashboards that inform organizational leadership and board committees about fundraising performance and donor trends.
* **Community Representation:** Represent Kids’ Meals at donor meetings, community gatherings, and special events with professionalism and enthusiasm.
* Other duties as assigned.

This position does not have direct employee reports.

*Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.*

**What We’re Looking For**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, marketing, or a related field required. An equivalent combination of relevant education and progressively responsible fundraising experience may be considered. CFRE certification is preferred.
* **Professional Experience:** At least ten years of progressive fundraising experience, including significant experience with individual and major gifts.
* **Fundraising Success:** Demonstrated success managing a donor portfolio and personally securing five\- and six\-figure gifts.
* **Portfolio Management:** Experience building donor pipelines and using moves management to advance prospects through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* **Strategic Leadership:** Ability to establish fundraising strategies, revenue projections, performance measures, and actionable plans aligned with organizational goals.
* **Relationship\-Building:** Strong interpersonal and emotional\-intelligence skills, with the ability to inspire and build trust with donors, board members, community leaders, and colleagues.
* **Communication:** Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and storytelling skills, with the ability to connect donor interests to meaningful impact.
* **CRM Experience:** Demonstrated experience using Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge, Bloomerang, Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, or a comparable donor\-management system.
* **Data\-Informed Decision\-Making:** Ability to analyze fundraising data, identify giving trends, evaluate performance, and translate findings into effective strategies.
* **Organization:** Exceptional planning, project\-management, and follow\-through skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
* **Mission Alignment:** A genuine commitment to ending childhood hunger and improving the well\-being of children and families.
* **Transportation:** A valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for local business\-related travel.

**Physical and Work Environment Requirements**

The position primarily operates in a professional office environment and requires regular local travel for donor meetings, community activities, and special events. Occasional extended periods of standing or walking and lifting or transporting materials weighing up to 25 pounds may be required.

jobs.description:
**Description**

  

The Attorney General is the chief legal officer of the State of Maryland. The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) has the general charge, supervision, and direction of the State's legal business, acting as legal advisors and representatives of the major agencies, various boards, commissions, officials, and institutions of State Government. The OAG also protects the public by civil enforcement of antitrust, civil rights, consumer protection, and securities laws and regulations and by the prosecution of organized crime, Medicaid fraud, environmental crimes, insurance fraud, state tax evasion, and other statutorily assigned matters. As Maryland's 47th Attorney General, Anthony G. Brown leads the Office with a critical focus on equity, justice, and fairness.  

The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General is seeking a strategic, experienced, and forward‑thinking operational leader to serve as Director of Operations. This is an exciting opportunity to help lead one of Maryland's largest and most impactful enforcement divisions. In FY25 alone, the Division received more than twelve thousand consumer complaints and sixty‑three thousand inquiries, recovering over twelve million dollars for Maryland consumers. With more than eighty attorneys, professionals, and volunteers, CPD operates from its Baltimore headquarters and maintains branch offices on the Eastern Shore, in Prince George's County, and in Western Maryland, providing both virtual and in‑person assistance across the State.


The Director of Operations works directly with the Chief of the Division and serves as her principal operational advisor. The Director is responsible for strengthening, streamlining, and modernizing the Division's administrative and operational infrastructure so that attorneys and staff can deliver high‑quality legal services efficiently and effectively. The Director oversees the Administrative Support Unit and the Registrations Unit and manages critical functions such as case management systems, outreach coordination, policy development and implementation, Executive Division coordination, hiring and retention, responses to public inquiries including Public Information Act requests, staff training and mentoring, employee engagement, internal communications, and publications and reports.


CPD's portfolio is broad and complex. The Division conducts major enforcement actions involving deceptive trade practices, adjudicates contested cases, mediates tens of thousands of consumer disputes each year, and oversees the Health Education and Advocacy Unit, which handles disputes involving medical billing, insurance coverage, and surprise medical bills. CPD also administers the Home Builder Registration and Guaranty Fund program, enforces data privacy laws such as the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act and the Maryland Kids Code, leads consumer outreach and education efforts statewide, and participates in multi‑state and federal enforcement collaborations. The Director plays a central role in supporting the operational needs of these units, which include arbitration, asset recovery, false claims, finance and lending, general enforcement, guaranty fund, health clubs, health education and advocacy, housing enforcement, home builders registration, identity theft, mediation, opioids enforcement, investigations, and administrative and operational functions.


The Director plans, directs, and coordinates operational activities across the Division, including modernization initiatives and organizational restructures. The role involves setting strategic goals, ensuring that operational teams have the resources they need, and establishing performance measures that support continuous improvement. The Director identifies and implements systems and technologies that enhance workflows and allow attorneys and staff to focus on core legal and enforcement work.


As a key member of the Chief's leadership team, the Director works closely with the Deputy Chiefs and Unit Chiefs to ensure that Division priorities move forward cohesively. The Director also helps shape CPD's work culture by promoting employee engagement, supporting training and development, and championing a positive, inclusive, and collaborative environment grounded in equity and innovation. The Director advises the Chief on budgets, public‑facing documents, hiring and personnel matters, organizational changes, and implementation of new policies and procedures. The role requires regular engagement with every unit within the Division and significant interaction with other State agencies, external partners, vendors, and members of the public.


This position offers a meaningful leadership opportunity for someone who thrives in a mission‑driven environment and is energized by complex operations, modernizing systems, and supporting teams that work every day to protect Maryland consumers. The Director of Operations plays a foundational role in ensuring that the Division has the clarity, structure, and momentum it needs to continue delivering high‑impact results for the State of Maryland.

 **Classification:** Admin Prog Mgr III  

  

**Experience:** The ideal candidate brings 8 years of progressively responsible experience in operations, business management, or administrative leadership, preferably within a legal, governmental, or public\-sector environment. They should have demonstrated success managing budgets, optimizing organizational processes, and navigating complex operational challenges. A bachelor's degree is required, and an MBA, MPA, or similar advanced degree is preferred. A JD, MBA, or some experience in the legal profession is also preferred.  

  

**Submission:** Applicants must submit a resume, cover letter, and a list of three professional references, including at least one current or former supervisor. Please note that this job posting will come offline at 6:00 p.m. EST on the closing date.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
Lead the Future of Senior Living in Nebraska
  
  

Nye Health Services is seeking an accomplished, strategic, and people\-centered Chief Operating Officer (COO) to help lead one of Nebraska's most respected senior living organizations into its next chapter of growth.
  
  

Reporting directly to the President and serving as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO will provide strategic and operational leadership across multiple service lines, including skilled nursing, assisted living, independent living, rehabilitation, outpatient therapy, memory care, and home health. This executive will play a pivotal role in developing leaders, strengthening operational performance, driving financial success, and ensuring exceptional experiences for residents, families, and team members.
  
  

This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact by leading a mission\-driven organization committed to innovation, operational excellence, and exceptional care.
  
  

About Nye Health Services
  
  

Headquartered in Fremont, Nebraska, Nye Health Services is a family\-owned senior living and healthcare organization serving more than 500 residents across multiple campuses throughout eastern Nebraska. With approximately 750 dedicated team members, Nye provides a full continuum of care, including independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, outpatient therapy, memory care, respite care, and home health services.
  
  

Our mission is to celebrate life by delivering exceptional service and superior value through innovative leadership in personalized care. We believe outstanding resident experiences begin with exceptional team experiences, and we've built a culture where people truly live—and work—happy.
  
  

What You'll Do
  
  

Strategic Leadership
  
  

* Partner with the President and Executive Leadership Team to execute organizational strategy and achieve long\-term goals.
* Lead enterprise\-wide operational initiatives that support growth, innovation, and organizational performance.
* Identify opportunities to improve systems, processes, and operational effectiveness across the organization.


Operational Excellence
  
  

* Provide executive oversight for multi\-site operations across senior living and healthcare services.
* Drive financial performance through census growth, labor optimization, operational efficiency, and fiscal stewardship.
* Ensure regulatory compliance, survey readiness, quality outcomes, and risk management across all service lines.


Leadership Development
  
  

* Coach, mentor, and develop Executive Directors and operational leaders.
* Build high\-performing teams and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Champion Nye's mission, values, and commitment to exceptional service.


What You'll Bring
  
  

* Ten or more years of progressive executive leadership experience in senior living, post\-acute care, healthcare, home health, or another complex multi\-site service organization or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Bachelor's degree required; master’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading large, multi\-site operations with responsibility for financial performance, growth, quality outcomes, and operational excellence.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, labor management, and strategic planning.
* Proven ability to develop leaders, build high\-performing teams, and drive organizational accountability.
* Experience navigating regulatory compliance, quality improvement, and risk management in highly regulated environments.
* Exceptional communication, relationship\-building, and change leadership skills.
* Current Nebraska licensure—or the ability to obtain applicable licensure—is preferred (such as Nursing Home Administrator or Assisted Living Administrator). Clinical licensure is welcomed but not required.

**WHO WE ARE**


EPC was conceived and operates to provide anyone who desires to provide for their families through the work they do, an opportunity to do so. Everything we do revolves around the vision of a company that provides safe, quality work, driving customer demand that ultimately results in the creation of new job opportunities in the markets we serve. The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day flow of all aspects of our business and carrying out the vision of the CEO. * Oversee day\-to\-day business functions and strategy, including human resources, operations, IT, maintenance, safety, and sales.

* Prepare and deliver operational reports and management reports.
* Establish KPI reporting and visibility across all departments.
* Identify and execute programs, software, automation, or other levels of optimization to improve organizational efficiencies.
* Ensure compliance on a company, state and federal level.
* Drive sustainable growth and minimize losses.
* Lead outreach and business relations.
* Consistent review of budgets across the organization to ensure alignment.

**WHAT WILL HELP YOU STAND OUT**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Construction, or related field
* MBA or other Master’s degree preferred.
* Diverse business knowledge related to Information Technology, Human Resources, Sales, Safety, and Operations is required.
* Strong analytical skills and strategic thinking abilities.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Superior Project Management skills and experience.
* Ability to lead and motivate cross\-functional teams to achieve project objectives.
* At least 15\+ years’ experience leading a mid\-size company in a high\-level role.
* Prior successful experience in the utilities construction or manufacturing industry is highly preferred.
* Project Management Professional or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification is highly preferred.

* Full\-time opportunity in a fast\-growth company!
* Opportunity to work autonomously. None of that micromanaging garbage. We hate that!
* Competitive pay plus incentives.

* Retirement benefits with company match.
* Company paid time\-off.
* Weekly paychecks!
* Career development and growth opportunities.

* This job will be primarily office\-based with exposure to normal office environments and noises.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO) – Skilled Nursing Operations
jobs.description:
**Chief Operating Officer (COO) – Skilled Nursing Operations**
==============================================================

**Location:** \[OKC, OK]  

**Employment Type:** Full\-Time  

**Reports To:** Ownership / CEO

**About the Opportunity**
-------------------------


We are seeking an experienced, hands\-on **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** to lead the operations of a growing portfolio of **skilled nursing facilities (SNFs)**.


This is a high\-impact leadership position for an experienced skilled nursing operator who understands what it takes to run **high\-quality, financially healthy, well\-managed nursing facilities**.


The ideal candidate may come from a **Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA), Regional Vice President of Operations, Regional Director of Operations, Executive Director, or similar skilled nursing leadership background**.


We are also open to candidates with a **CFO, finance, or healthcare finance background** who have substantial experience with skilled nursing operations and understand how staffing, census, reimbursement, quality, and operational decisions drive facility financial performance.


This is not a purely corporate or administrative role. The COO will be expected to **know what is happening inside each building, understand the numbers, hold leadership accountable, identify problems quickly, and drive measurable improvement.**

**What You'll Own**
-------------------


The COO will have overall responsibility for the operational and financial performance of seven skilled nursing facilities.


Key areas of responsibility include:

* Provide leadership and accountability for all seven facilities.
* Partner with and hold Administrators, DONs, and facility leadership teams accountable for results.
* Establish clear operating standards and consistent expectations across the portfolio.
* Monitor facility performance through regular operational and financial reviews.
* Drive census growth, occupancy, admissions, and referral development.
* Manage labor costs, staffing levels, overtime, agency utilization, and productivity.
* Review facility P\&Ls and identify opportunities to improve revenue, margins, and operating performance.
* Monitor key financial and operational metrics and translate data into action.
* Identify underperforming facilities and develop specific turnaround plans.
* Ensure facilities maintain strong clinical, quality, and regulatory performance.

**The Opportunity**

What if fundraising were about more than raising money?

What if it were about helping people find a place in something they care about?

Evergreen Christian Outreach (EChO) is looking for a **Director of Development** who sees fundraising that way.

For more than 35 years, EChO has walked alongside individuals and families in Evergreen and the surrounding mountain communities, helping people move from survival toward greater stability and success. Today, our work includes food access, shelter, client services, housing and utility assistance, employment support, volunteer engagement, ReSale Shop and more.

We are now entering an exciting next chapter.

EChO has an extraordinary history of community support. Individuals, families, businesses, congregations, foundations, volunteers, and community organizations have invested their time, resources, relationships, and generosity in EChO for decades.

**Our opportunity now is to build on that foundation.**

We are seeking a **Director of Development** to lead that effort, to strengthen the systems behind our development work, grow contributed revenue, and, most importantly, deepen EChO’s relationships with the people and organizations who care about our community.

We are looking for someone who understands that people rarely connect with an organization simply because they received a good fundraising appeal.

They connect because something matters to them.

Maybe they have a personal connection to hunger or housing insecurity. Maybe they care deeply about their mountain community. Maybe they want to make a difference for families. Maybe they are looking for a meaningful way to use their resources, relationships, skills, or time.

**Your job will be to listen, discover what matters to people, and help them find meaningful ways to be part of EChO’s work.**

We think of this as building a **community of generosity**.

Generosity can mean a financial gift, but it can also mean volunteering, making an introduction, sharing expertise, advocating for our mission, opening a door, providing resources, or simply standing with EChO and the people we serve.

The Director of Development will help create opportunities for all of those forms of generosity.

· **Lead fundraising campaigns.** Develop and manage annual and special campaigns in partnership with Marketing \& Communications.

· **Strengthen engagement.** Create meaningful experiences that help people connect with EChO, understand our impact, and find ways to participate.

· **Build a culture of generosity.** Work with the Executive Director, Board, staff, and volunteers so that development becomes a shared organizational responsibility—not something that belongs only to the development function.

· **Build the infrastructure.** Strengthen EChO’s development systems, database, stewardship practices, prospect management, reporting, and use of data.

· **Think strategically about the future.** Build a development program and **team** that can grow with EChO and increasingly engage people beyond the organization’s existing relationships.

This is a role for someone who is comfortable moving between **strategy and relationships, big\-picture thinking and hands\-on execution**.

**Who You’ll Work With**

The Director of Development reports to the Executive Director and works closely with EChO’s Board of Directors, leadership team, staff, volunteers, and community partners.

You will also become a visible and trusted representative of EChO in the community.

This is an opportunity to work alongside people who care deeply about EChO and the people we serve, and to help bring even more people into that community.

**POSITION SUMMARY**



This position supports the work of the Y, a leading nonprofit, charitable organization committed to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living and social responsibility. The Development Director at the Akron Area YMCA provides leadership in financial development to advance the YMCAs mission through annual giving, government and foundation grants, endowment bequests and gifts, and capital fundraising campaigns. The Development Director assists in developing actively engaged volunteers and staff members who actively participate in fundraising efforts and who represent the YMCA as a community convener and collaborator to address critical social issues.

Our mission and core values are brought to life by our culture. In the Y, we strive to live our cause of strengthening communities with purpose and intentionality every day. We are welcoming: we are open to all. We are a place where you can belong and become. We are genuine: we value you and embrace your individuality. We are hopeful: we believe in you and your potential to become a catalyst in the world. We are nurturing: we support you in your journey to develop your full potential. We are determined: above all else, we are on a relentless quest to make our community stronger beginning with you.

* Develop and implement a comprehensive annual plan which helps maintain the fiscal health of the organization and provides future financial resources for growth and expansion. Ensures fundraising activities and strategies are sufficient to support the Y’s charitable needs.
* **Program/Project Management:** Develops organizational goals and strategic plans, balancing long\-term direction and short\-term requirements.
