jobs.title: Director of Government Relations
jobs.description:
**Your career has a home here.**

Ready to make an impact with a dynamic, forward\-thinking company?


As a leading property manager of single\-family rental homes nationwide, we take great pride in creating an enjoyable living experience for our residents – and an empowering, people\-first culture for our team members. That’s why, for two years in a row, our employees have voted Progress a certified Great Place to Work®.


**Why join Progress?**

As the demand for professionally managed rental homes continues to grow, so do the opportunities at Progress. We’re looking for passionate professionals who are ready to grow with us, make a difference and be part of something meaningful.

**Want to learn more?**

Text “ProgressJobs” to 25000 to chat with Kate, our AI Recruiting Assistant. She can help you explore open roles, apply, and answer your questions in real time.

**Job Summary:**


The Director of Government Relations will represent Progress Residential (“Progress”) by advocating before state and local government officials on policies relevant to Progress Residential, its affiliates, Owners, and Property Managers in the Single\-Family Rental (“SFR”) industry. Reporting to the Vice President of Government Affairs, the Director will be responsible for executing government relations strategies, influencing key decision\-makers, building durable relationships, and effectively communicating Progress’ and/or the industry’s positions before state and local governments, with limited federal engagement as needed.


This role requires a disciplined operator who can manage issues independently while remaining closely aligned with the Vice President of Government Affairs.

**Essential Functions:**

* Monitor and analyze state and local legislative and regulatory proposals affecting Progress and/or the SFR industry.
* Assess the potential impact of proposed policies on Progress, the SFR industry, and customers, and elevate risks early.
* Develop and implement advocacy strategies and policy positions in coordination with the Vice President of Government Affairs.
* Collaborate closely with internal teams and external consultants to ensure consistent, effective advocacy.
* Establish and maintain strong working relationships with legislators, policymakers, regulators, and government staff.
* Educate and persuade key decision\-makers regarding the SFR industry’s role, concerns, and economic contributions.
* Support efforts to influence the development, modification, and implementation of laws and regulations affecting Progress.
* Advocate for policies that promote fair competition, economic growth, and operational stability.
* Cultivate relationships with industry leaders, member companies, and relevant advocacy organizations.
* Coordinate with other lobbyists and stakeholders to form alliances and coalitions in support of shared policy objectives.
* Represent Progress in industry meetings, conferences, and public forums as directed.
* Prepare senior leadership and market teams for meetings with government officials and regulatory agencies.
* Serve as a reliable surrogate for the Vice President of Government Affairs when appropriate.


Qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in political science, public policy, economics, or a related field preferred (Post\-Graduate degree strongly preferred).
* 7–10 years of experience in government relations, public policy, government service, or a related role; Capitol Hill or state legislative experience required.
* Working knowledge of the single\-family rental industry, housing policy, or regulated real estate sectors.
* Strong understanding of legislative processes, regulatory frameworks, and political dynamics at the state and local levels.
* Proven ability to analyze complex policy issues and translate them into clear advocacy strategies.
* Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
* Demonstrated ability to build, manage, and sustain relationships with policymakers and stakeholders.
* High ethical standards and a demonstrated commitment to compliance with lobbying laws and disclosure requirements.

**What you can expect from us:**

* **Competitive Compensation** \- Including performance\-based bonuses that reward your contributions.
* **Comprehensive Benefits Package** \- Medical, dental, vision, parental leave, 401(k) with company match and more.
* **Generous Time Off** – Enjoy PTO based on tenure, 13 paid holidays and 1 floating holiday.
* **Ongoing Learning and Development** \- Quarterly summits, town hall meetings and continuous training to support your professional growth.
* **A Culture that Celebrates You** \- We believe in collaboration, recognition and having fun while doing important work.

This summary is not an all\-inclusive description of job duties. Other job duties and responsibilities may also be assigned by the incumbent’s supervisor at any time based upon Company need.


Employment with Progress Residential is conditional on a satisfactory background and drug screen.


Progress Residential is a proud Equal Opportunity employer, m/f/d/v.

jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
The Peoria Riverfront Museum—**the only multidisciplinary museum of its kind in the nation**—is seeking a bold, strategic, and creative leader to serve as our next **Director of Marketing and Communications**.

This is not simply a marketing role. It is an opportunity to shape the voice and visibility of a dynamic cultural institution that seamlessly integrates **art, science, history, achievement, and cinema** under one roof. The Director will champion our brand, energize our audiences, and position the Museum as an essential cultural destination locally, regionally, and nationally.

If you are a visionary storyteller who thrives at the intersection of strategy, creativity, and leadership—this is your stage.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads the development and execution of the Museum’s comprehensive external marketing and communications strategy. This role drives brand awareness, audience engagement, attendance growth, media visibility, and revenue support.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director oversees media relations, advertising, digital strategy, website management, social media, graphic design, and all external communications. The role also leads the marketing team, manages budgets, evaluates campaign performance, and ensures that every public\-facing message reflects the excellence and innovation of the Museum.

**Strategic Leadership**

**Brand and Content Excellence**

* Lead the creation and curation of compelling content across print, digital, video, and social platforms.
* Oversee production of brochures, publications, website content, social campaigns, signage, photography, and multimedia assets.
* Ensure brand consistency and high visual standards across all channels.
* Ensure marketing materials meet accessibility standards and reflect the Museum's commitment to serving diverse audiences.

**Digital and Media Presence**

* Manage the Museum’s website strategy, design, and maintenance to ensure a dynamic and user\-friendly experience.
* Drive social media engagement and digital storytelling initiatives.
* Cultivate strong relationships with local, regional, and national media to secure impactful coverage.

**Advertising and Vendor Management**

* Strategically purchase and manage advertising across traditional and digital platforms.
* Oversee relationships with creative agencies, designers, printers, and other vendors.

**Measurement and Impact**

* Implement evaluation tools to measure marketing effectiveness.
* Analyze data, interpret campaign results, and adjust strategy for maximum impact.
* Align marketing performance with institutional goals for attendance, membership, and revenue.

**Team and Department Leadership**

* Lead a highly performing team and oversee day\-to\-day operations of the Marketing and Communications Department.
* Lead budgeting, planning, staff supervision, and professional development.
* Oversee departmental hiring, performance management, coaching, disciplinary action and annual evaluations.
* Collaborate with the COO and Director of Finance to develop and manage the annual marketing budget.

**Who You Are**

You are both strategist and storyteller. You understand how to translate mission into message and ideas into action. You thrive in fast\-paced, creative environments and bring energy, organization, and leadership to everything you do.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree required (Journalism, Communications, Marketing, or related field preferred).
* Minimum five years of experience writing and editing across print and digital platforms.
* Demonstrated success developing and implementing marketing strategies with measurable results.
* Exceptional writing, editing, and visual storytelling skills.
* Strong knowledge of local, regional, and national media landscapes.
* Experience managing advertising and vendor relationships.
* Ability to evaluate and integrate innovative media technologies.
* Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines.
* Collaborative leadership style with supervisory experience preferred.
* Nonprofit experience preferred.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and standard business applications.

**Work Environment and Physical Requirements**

* Ability to work in a standard office environment using computers and other office equipment for extended periods.
* Visual acuity for reviewing detailed creative work.
* Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and in writing.
* Ability to move throughout the Museum and event spaces to attend meetings and support programs and special events.
* Ability to occasionally lift and carry materials weighing up to 30 pounds.
* Ability to work evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed to support Museum operations and events.
* Ability to travel occasionally for meetings, conferences, and professional development.

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

*The Peoria Riverfront Museum is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.*

**Why Join the Peoria Riverfront Museum?**

The Peoria Riverfront Museum is a cultural catalyst creating transformative experiences for our community. As the only museum in the country to unite art, science, history, and achievement in a single institution of its scale, we are redefining what a museum can be.

As Director of Marketing and Communications, you will not just promote programs—you will help shape the cultural narrative of an entire region.

If you are ready to lead boldly, think creatively, and make measurable impact, we invite you to apply.

jobs.description:
**Salary Grade**
----------------

  


Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary range available for this position at the time of its posting. The salary range is between $82,862 and $104,821, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.


Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.


**Job Description**
-------------------

  


POSITION OBJECTIVE


The Director of Marketing and Communications of the National Science Foundation (NSF) NEO\-SMART Engine in Northeast Ohio (NEO\-SMART) is responsible for building and stewarding the NEO\-SMART's public identity, brand, and communications strategy. Reporting to the Chief Operations Officer, this role serves as NEO\-SMARTs chief storyteller and brand architect\-creating, implementing, and executing integrated marketing and communications strategies that increase the visibility and enhance the reputation of NEO\-SMART among its diverse stakeholder communities, including regional partners, NSF, industry, government, media, and the broader public.


NEO\-SMART is a U.S. National Science Foundation Regional Innovation Engine, led by Case Western Reserve University and backed by an NSF investment of up to $160 million over ten years. It unites 70\+ partners across Northeast Ohio\-Cleveland, Akron, Canton, and Youngstown\-to move materials innovation from the lab to the factory floor: funding use\-inspired research and development, commercializing new materials and processes, and building the skilled workforce to make them. The director is a pivotal connector, bridging NEO\-SMART's programmatic work with the audiences who need to know about it\-translating complex science, technology, and economic development activities into compelling narratives that drive awareness, engagement, and support. The ideal candidate is a strategic communications professional with experience in multi\-channel marketing, content development, brand management, and media relations, and who brings a genuine passion for NEO\-SMART's mission in Northeast Ohio.

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

* Develop and lead implementation of a comprehensive, integrated marketing and communications strategy for NEO\-SMART, aligned with the strategic plan and NSF cooperative agreement requirements; establish annual goals, key messages, and priority audiences. Work with NEO\-SMART leadership to prioritize communications initiatives based on strategic importance, partner needs, and available resources; monitor outcomes and adjust tactics as needed to maximize impact and reach. Uphold and evolve NEO\-SMART¿s brand standards, including visual identity, voice, and messaging guidelines, ensuring consistency across all internal and external communications and all partner\-produced materials generated by the Engine's coalition of 70\+ partner organizations. (35%)
* Lead development and ongoing management of all NEO\-SMART\-owned communications channels, including the website, social media platforms, email newsletters, and digital publications; ensure content is timely, accurate, audience\-appropriate, and on\-brand. Research, write, and edit a broad range of communications content, including news releases, feature stories, partner spotlights, executive communications, program summaries, annual reports, and NSF\-facing reporting content that highlights NEO\-SMART milestones and outcomes. Commission, manage, and coordinate with external vendors and freelancers (designers, photographers, videographers, and web developers) to produce high\-quality creative assets that support NEO\-SMART programs and events, administering an annual marketing and communications budget. (35%)
* Develop and maintain relationships with local, regional, and national media outlets; proactively pitch stories about NEO\-SMART research breakthroughs, workforce development milestones, community partnerships, and economic impact; manage all inbound media inquiries. Prepare NEO\-SMART leadership and spokespeople for media appearances, public presentations, and congressional or NSF briefings, including developing talking points, background materials, and presentation decks. Represent the NEO\-SMART¿s communications function at partner events, NSF program convenings, and regional stakeholder meetings as needed. (15%)
* Plan and execute communications support for NEO\-SMART events, including symposia, industry showcases, workforce program launches, community convenings, and annual partner meetings; develop event messaging, promotional materials, invitations, and post\-event coverage. Collaborate with pillar program managers to develop audience\-specific communications for use\-inspired research, commercialization and adoption, workforce development, and economic growth. (10%)


NONESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


Perform other duties as assigned. (5%)

  

CONTACTS


Department: Regular contact NEO\-SMART chief executive officer, chief operating officer, chief research and translation officer, pillar directors, and NEO\-SMART team members (content development, strategic messaging, event communications, leadership preparation).


University: Contact with all departments and faculty related to NEO\-SMART to communicate around programs and projects. Regular contact with communications and marketing offices (co\-branded communications, partner story development, joint event promotion).


External: Regular contact with communications and marketing offices at other partner institutions, media contacts, industry partners, community organizations, external vendors and freelancers (media relations, content production, event promotion, stakeholder communications).


Students: Occasional (through workforce program promotion, student spotlight content, and ecosystem\-building events)

This role is responsible for day\-to\-day operations and long\-term sustainability. This is a full‑time (40 hours), exempt leadership position that reports directly to the Board of Directors

Executive Director Responsibilities

* Provide community and agency leadership to ensure FnG’s mission is effectively implemented across all programs and initiatives.
* Ensure fiscal accountability in collaboration with the agency’s bookkeeper, Treasurer, and Board of Directors, including budget development and monitoring, grant reporting, and administration of donor and grant funds.
* Develop and execute strategic plans together with the Board, staff, and community partners focusing on FnG’s mission, goals, and sustainability.
* Oversee daily operations and program delivery, including community education and outreach, shelter and hotline services, case management, and other survivor support programs.
* Cultivate a trauma\-informed, inclusive, and equitable workplace culture that promotes the provision of trauma\-informed services for survivors, staff well\-being, and retention of skilled staff.
* Manage the Recruitment, training, supervision, and mentorship of staff and volunteers to provide high\-quality services to survivors and the community.
* Uphold best practices in trauma\-informed service delivery for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and other forms of intimate violence.
* Maintain confidentiality across settings, including employment records, client services, and organizational matters.
* Strengthen and expand partnerships with community organizations, funders, government, and law enforcement to coordinate services for the benefit of survivors.
* Lead fundraising and development efforts with the Board of Directors, including donor cultivation, grant development, and major events to secure and diversify revenue.

* Manage complex organizational projects and systems improvements, ensuring effective planning, resource allocation, and timely project completion.
* Serve as the public leader for FnG and its mission by building community relationships and advocating for the agency and its mission in public settings.
* Promote policies and programs that ensure strong succession planning, leadership development, organizational stability, and the long\-term provision of mission\-focused services and programs.

Required Qualifications

* Arizona DPS Level One Fingerprint Clearance Card
* The Executive Director must uphold the highest standards of confidentiality in accordance with federal and state laws, including VAWA, FVPSA, VOCA and HIPAA‑related provisions where applicable. This role requires strict protection of all survivor information, organizational records, and sensitive operational data. The Executive Director will ensure that no personally identifiable information (PII), case details, or client‑related communications are disclosed without legally permissible authorization.
* Professional experience working with survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and other forms of intimate violence or another closely related human services area.

Preferred Qualifications

* Master’s degree or equivalent experience.
* Experience supervising direct service teams and implementing trauma\-informed practices.
* Experience managing capital campaigns or major development projects.

**The Berkshire Immigrant Center (BIC) is seeking a Development Director** to join our leadership team and oversee all fundraising efforts. This role combines strategic planning with hands\-on execution and offers the opportunity to make a meaningful, community\-facing impact in support of BIC’s mission.

As immigration processes grow more complex, fundraising helps BIC sustain and expand access to immigration legal services, keep the community informed, and adapt programs as needs evolve. Philanthropy keeps client costs low, supports free citizenship preparation classes, and increases emergency assistance for basic needs such as rent, utilities, and application fees. It also strengthens BIC’s long\-term sustainability by expanding our immigration legal capacity, deepening statewide connections, and building the resources that uniquely position us to serve immigrant families across the region.

Fundraising at BIC is a shared effort. The Executive Director (ED) is actively involved in major donor strategy, solicitations, and grant development, while the Board supports cultivation and outreach. The Development Director reports directly to the ED and is supported by a part\-time Development Assistant.

We are seeking a highly organized, detail\-oriented professional who excels at building meaningful relationships with donors, volunteers, and committees. **BIC seeks to raise over $1,000,000 this fiscal year**, primarily through private donations from individuals, companies, and foundations.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Partner with the Board of Trustees, ED, and Development and Benefit Committees to design and implement a comprehensive development program that increases annual revenue.
* In alignment with the Strategic Plan, help develop and implement a long\-term fundraising strategy with the ED and external consultant.
* Meet regularly with the ED to review progress toward goals, monitor revenue, and adjust priorities as needed.
* Lead execution of the Annual Appeal and a signature spring fundraising event

* Cultivate and steward donors while managing a portfolio of prospects and supporters
* Research prospective funders; write and submit grant proposals and reports; and maintain strong relationships with foundation and institutional funders.
* Support communications and campaign messaging across email, social media, and other channels.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
* 3\-5 years of nonprofit development experience with demonstrated fundraising execution.
* Proven success securing grants and individual gifts in the four\- and five\-figure range
* Experience planning and executing an Annual Appeal and one signature fundraising event.
* Strong writing and editing skills for proposals, appeals, and donor communications.
* Proficiency with Little Green Light or other constituency management system.
* Strong project management skills, ability to prioritize and manage multiple deadlines.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the ED, Board, and volunteers.
* Commitment to ethical, non\-extractive storytelling, client confidentiality, and cultural humility in an immigrant\-serving context.
* Familiarity with local and regional funders is a plus.
* Multilingual skills, particularly Spanish, are a plus.
* Strong project management and organizational skills, ability to prioritize and manage multiple deadlines.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the Executive Director, Board, and volunteers.
* Commitment to ethical, non\-extractive storytelling, client confidentiality, and cultural humility in an immigrant\-serving context.
* Familiarity with Berkshire County and Massachusetts funders and community networks is a plus.
* Multilingual skills, particularly Spanish, are a plus.

**To Apply**

Interested candidates can either submit a cover letter or choose to answer any of the following questions:

* How do you approach donor and grant storytelling for immigrant\-serving work in a way that is accurate, dignified, and non\-extractive? Share a brief example.
* Tell us about a fundraising initiative you planned and executed end to end at a small or mid\-sized nonprofit. What was your role, what systems or tools did you use (CRM, calendars, stewardship plans), and what were the results? Please include specific outcomes if available.

**Please submit the cover letter or answers along with a resume to Megan Donovan at megan@chestnutconsultingllc.com**. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

**\-\-\-\-\-\-**  
**Berkshire Immigrant Center** 

The mission of the Berkshire Immigrant Center (BIC) is to advocate for the rights of immigrants by helping them navigate the U.S. immigration system through affordable legal services, education, and access to local resources. Our work helps individuals and families overcome financial and cultural barriers while strengthening civic engagement and expanding opportunity in our community.

BIC serves more than 800 individuals annually from over 60 countries in several languages. We are the only nonprofit in Berkshire County recognized by the U.S. Department of Justice to provide immigration legal services. Founded in 1997, BIC became an independent 501(c)(3\) organization in 2021\.

*BIC is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.*

new_jobs.description:
The Urban Land Institute is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit research and education organization supported by its members. Founded in 1936, the Institute has more than 48,000 members worldwide representing the full spectrum of land use and real estate development disciplines across private enterprise and public service. ULI’s mission is to shape the future of the built environment for transformative impact in communities worldwide.

**About ULI Kansas City**


ULI Kansas City is the Institute’s home in one of the Midwest’s most dynamic real estate markets, connecting developers, investors, designers, public officials, and civic leaders around the region’s biggest land use questions. Through signature programs like the quarterly Envision series, Technical Assistance Panels, and member\-led committees spanning Young Leaders, Emerging Developers, and REDI, the council shapes how Kansas City grows.


The council is entering a defining new chapter. In early 2027, the ULI Nebraska satellite will transition into an independent Local Organizing Committee, and ULI Kansas City will move forward as a focused, city\-anchored district council. That change creates a rare leadership moment: the chance to rebuild the council’s committee structure, re\-energize its membership, and set the direction for what ULI Kansas City becomes next.

**The Role**


This is a leadership role built around relationships and ownership. Reporting to the Senior Director, District Councils, and working in close partnership with the District Council Chair and a highly engaged member leadership, the Interim Executive Director owns the council’s program of work end to end: strategy, programming, membership, sponsorship, communications, and operations.


The mandate is clear: guide the council smoothly through the Nebraska transition, grow membership and revenue in the Kansas City market, and build the platform for the council’s next stage. The leader in this seat will directly shape ULI Kansas City’s long\-term structure and direction.


This is a full\-time, benefits\-eligible interim appointment of approximately 12 months. Based on the council’s performance through the transition, including membership and revenue growth, ULI may consider establishing a permanent Executive Director role at the end of the term. This appointment is interim, and conversion or continued employment beyond the term is not guaranteed.

* Lead ULI Kansas City through the transition of the ULI Nebraska satellite to an independent Local Organizing Committee, managing member communications, programming continuity, and financial planning through the change.

* Grow sponsorship, grant, and program revenue against defined revenue and membership targets.
* Establish ULI Kansas City’s identity and program of work as a standalone, city\-focused district council.

* Develop and implement a strategic program of work, budget, and staffing plan with clearly defined outcomes and methods to measure success.
* Oversee all district council committees, including Management, Programs, Membership Engagement, Young Leaders, Emerging Developers, REDI, TAPs (Technical Assistance Panels), and Sponsorship; engage existing volunteers and create new opportunities for active member involvement.
* Support the Chair, Advisory, Management, Governance, and other leadership committees, building out administration, leadership development, and succession planning.
* Oversee programs, communications, social media, and reporting, including the quarterly Envision program series.
* Develop and manage event and committee budgets, including forecasting, tracking, and reconciliation.

**Relationships \& Sponsorship**

* Build strong relationships within the Kansas City community and with ULI Americas/Global and other district councils.
* Work directly with ULI members, including Advisory Board and Management Committee members, member firms, sponsors, prospects, vendors, partner organizations, and consultants.
* Build funding relationships and strategic partnerships with existing sponsors, expand the sponsor network, and pursue and manage grant applications.

**Staff Leadership**

* Direct and develop ULI Kansas City’s part\-time contractor

**What are we looking for?**

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree required, and/or 5\+ years of related nonprofit or membership organization experience.
* Demonstrated ability to grow and retain membership and generate revenue through sponsorship, grants, and programs.
* Ability to plan and oversee high\-quality events, and to work effectively with diverse groups of people, including members, corporate leaders, politicians, educators, public officials, and ULI national staff.
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple concurrent workstreams with responsible follow\-through.
* Strong oral and written communication skills, and strong organizational and time management skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint), SharePoint, and Zoom.

**Preferred**

**Title:** Executive Director

**Reports to:** Board of Directors

**F.L.S.A. Status:** Full\-time, Exempt

**ORGANIZATION**

Mason EDC promotes the economic vitality and growth of Mason County by cultivating partnership among industry, government, labor, and education. The organization works to recruit new business investment, retain and expand existing employers, and support entrepreneurs, while encouraging quality job opportunities and preserving the county's environmental and community character.

As the state designated Associate Development Organization (ADO) for Mason County and a 501(c)(6\) nonprofit organization. It is governed by a Board of Directors that draws together public officials and private sector leaders, operating with the independence of the private sector while carrying out a publicly designated economic development role.

**GENERAL FUNCTION**

The Executive Director serves as Mason EDC's chief strategist, spokesperson, and organizational leader. The role calls for a strong strategic planner who can translate the Board's priorities into action, a skilled convener and collaborator who brings business, government, and community partners to the same table. The ideal candidate is a creative, solutions\-oriented problem solver comfortable pursuing new opportunities on behalf of Mason County. The Executive Director serves as the primary communication link between the Board of Directors and Mason EDC’s staff.

The Executive Director is expected to be proactive and entrepreneurial in identifying opportunities for Mason County's economic growth, bringing the energy of a recruiter to attract new investment, talent, and partnerships. The role is also responsible for leading and developing Mason EDC's staff, ensuring the organization has the internal capacity and culture needed to carry out its mission.

**JOB DUTIES \& OBJECTIVES**

* Leads the development, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of Mason EDC's strategic plan, including business retention, expansion, and recruitment initiatives.
* Serves as Mason County's principal liaison connecting local businesses, prospective investors, government partners, and community organizations.
* Regularly interacts with elected officials, government staff, business leaders, and community members, including situations where relationships or priorities may be challenging to navigate.
* Functions as the local economic development administrator for grant\-funded programs, guiding the pursuit, management, and compliance reporting associated with state, federal, and foundation funding.
* Provides pro\-business policy advisory and advocacy on behalf of Mason County businesses and partner agencies at the local, regional, and state level, including legislative priorities.
* Leads market analysis to identify trends, opportunities, and barriers to growth across the county's core industries, as well as emerging sectors.
* Ensures compliance with Mason EDC's 501(c)(6\) obligations, funding agreements, procurement policy, and organizational bylaws.
* Partners with accounting staff and the Finance Committee to provide timely financial reporting to the Board and to develop an annual budget that supports the organization's long\-term fiscal sustainability.
* Recruits new members and leads fundraising initiatives to meet operational expenses.
* Negotiates contracts and partnership agreements on behalf of the organization.
* Maintains confidentiality of restricted or private information and records and effectively handles sensitive matters.
* Communicates regularly with the Board of Directors, ensuring a clear understanding of current finances, projects, and programs.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Directly supervises Mason EDC staff across its core functions, including business development, external affairs, program management, and accounting, along with any part\-time staff, contractors, and interns.
* Sets clear expectations, provides regular feedback, and conducts performance evaluations.
* Builds a collaborative, growth\-oriented team culture.
* Oversees hiring, onboarding, and staff development planning.
* Delegates program and project responsibilities appropriately.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

*Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities*

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects and competing priorities in a fast\-paced environment.
* Knowledge of nonprofit budgeting, accounting principles, and federal funding compliance requirements.

*Education \& Experience*

* Bachelor's degree in business management, public administration, economic development, or a related field. Equivalent professional experience may substitute for formal education.
* A minimum of five (5\) years of progressively responsible leadership experience in economic development or community development, including experience in an executive\-level role.
* Demonstrated experience in fiscal and contract management, nonprofit finance, and procurement policy.

The Economic Development Council of Mason County is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Pay: $110,000\.00 \- $135,000\.00 per year

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

The Tennessee Aquarium is seeking an accomplished, strategic, and highly collaborative Chief Operating Officer to help lead one of the nation’s most respected aquariums through an ambitious new era of growth and impact.



Located on the banks of the Tennessee River in downtown Chattanooga, the Tennessee Aquarium is a nationally recognized leader in freshwater conservation, education, research, and exceptional guest experiences. Since opening in 1992, the Aquarium has welcomed millions of visitors, helped catalyze Chattanooga’s celebrated riverfront renaissance, and built an extraordinary reputation for connecting people with nature and protecting the remarkable freshwater biodiversity of the Southeast.



Today, the Aquarium is building on that strong foundation while intentionally shifting its focus from business maintenance to impact growth. A new strategic platform is nearing completion, a ten\-year facilities master planning process is on the horizon, and significant investments are underway in veterinary medicine, conservation science, education, guest experiences, and organizational capacity. In 2025, the Aquarium welcomed more than 784,000 guests while continuing to achieve strong financial, conservation, and educational results.


**The Opportunity**



Reporting to President \& CEO Andy Wood, the Chief Operating Officer will serve as a key strategic and operating partner, helping translate the Aquarium’s ambitious vision into coordinated action.



This is much more than a traditional operations role. The COO will oversee a broad portfolio of functions while helping ensure that the people, systems, facilities, resources, and organizational capacity are in place to support the Aquarium’s next phase of growth. The role will influence guest experience and earned revenue; facilities and major capital projects; leadership development and organizational culture; safety, risk, and business continuity; long\-term exhibit and facilities planning; and implementation of the Aquarium’s emerging strategic plan.



The successful candidate will also play an important role in strengthening collaboration and accountability across a highly specialized organization and developing the next generation of Aquarium leaders. This individual will serve as a trusted partner to a visionary, energetic CEO — bringing sound judgment, prioritization, candid counsel, disciplined execution, and the ability to turn ambitious ideas into measurable results.


**Key Responsibilities**



The Chief Operating Officer will:


* Translate strategic vision into clear priorities, operating plans, and measurable results.
* Lead guest\-facing operations with a strong focus on hospitality, attendance, earned revenue growth, and exceptional guest experiences.
* Provide executive leadership for facilities, infrastructure, major capital projects, operational safety, disaster preparedness, and business continuity.
* Partner in the development of the Aquarium’s ten\-year facilities master plan and long\-term exhibit priorities.
* Develop leaders, strengthen management capabilities, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, hospitality, and shared purpose.
* Help lead the organization thoughtfully through growth and change while preserving the strengths of an already successful institution.
* Strengthen cross\-functional coordination and help highly specialized teams operate around shared organizational priorities.
* Serve as a respected representative of the Tennessee Aquarium within the Association of Zoos \& Aquariums and the broader professional community.


**The Successful Candidate**



Strong candidates will bring:


* Seven or more years of senior leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading complex, multi\-functional operations and senior\-level teams.
* Experience in an executive leadership position with a cultural institution is strongly preferred.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, P\&L responsibility, revenue generation, resource allocation, and expense management.
* A record of translating strategy and vision into disciplined execution.
* Exceptional judgment and the confidence to serve as a genuine operating partner to a CEO.
* High emotional intelligence and demonstrated success developing leaders, building trust, and navigating different personalities and perspectives.
* Experience guiding organizations and teams through meaningful growth and change.
* Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively with a Board, executive colleagues, employees at all levels, and external stakeholders.
* A genuine commitment to the Aquarium’s mission and an understanding of how operational excellence, guest experience, revenue, conservation, and education work together to advance impact.


A bachelor’s degree is required; an advanced degree is preferred.

Chattanooga combines an exceptional quality of life with an increasingly dynamic economy. **Job Summary:** The Director of Development is responsible for supporting the GHS mission and vision through acquisition of funding necessary to expand and sustain GHS programs. This person will maintain a high level of understanding of the GHS model and exhibit passion for the GHS mission and oversee development and implementation of annual and campaign\-specific fundraising plans designed to obtain philanthropic gifts to advance the GHS research and educational mission. new_jobs.title: Director of Operations, Consumer Protection Division
new_jobs.description:
**Description**

  

The Attorney General is the chief legal officer of the State of Maryland. The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) has the general charge, supervision, and direction of the State's legal business, acting as legal advisors and representatives of the major agencies, various boards, commissions, officials, and institutions of State Government. The OAG also protects the public by civil enforcement of antitrust, civil rights, consumer protection, and securities laws and regulations and by the prosecution of organized crime, Medicaid fraud, environmental crimes, insurance fraud, state tax evasion, and other statutorily assigned matters. As Maryland's 47th Attorney General, Anthony G. Brown leads the Office with a critical focus on equity, justice, and fairness.  

The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General is seeking a strategic, experienced, and forward‑thinking operational leader to serve as Director of Operations. This is an exciting opportunity to help lead one of Maryland's largest and most impactful enforcement divisions. In FY25 alone, the Division received more than twelve thousand consumer complaints and sixty‑three thousand inquiries, recovering over twelve million dollars for Maryland consumers. With more than eighty attorneys, professionals, and volunteers, CPD operates from its Baltimore headquarters and maintains branch offices on the Eastern Shore, in Prince George's County, and in Western Maryland, providing both virtual and in‑person assistance across the State.


The Director of Operations works directly with the Chief of the Division and serves as her principal operational advisor. The Director is responsible for strengthening, streamlining, and modernizing the Division's administrative and operational infrastructure so that attorneys and staff can deliver high‑quality legal services efficiently and effectively. The Director oversees the Administrative Support Unit and the Registrations Unit and manages critical functions such as case management systems, outreach coordination, policy development and implementation, Executive Division coordination, hiring and retention, responses to public inquiries including Public Information Act requests, staff training and mentoring, employee engagement, internal communications, and publications and reports.


CPD's portfolio is broad and complex. The Division conducts major enforcement actions involving deceptive trade practices, adjudicates contested cases, mediates tens of thousands of consumer disputes each year, and oversees the Health Education and Advocacy Unit, which handles disputes involving medical billing, insurance coverage, and surprise medical bills. CPD also administers the Home Builder Registration and Guaranty Fund program, enforces data privacy laws such as the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act and the Maryland Kids Code, leads consumer outreach and education efforts statewide, and participates in multi‑state and federal enforcement collaborations. The Director plays a central role in supporting the operational needs of these units, which include arbitration, asset recovery, false claims, finance and lending, general enforcement, guaranty fund, health clubs, health education and advocacy, housing enforcement, home builders registration, identity theft, mediation, opioids enforcement, investigations, and administrative and operational functions.


The Director plans, directs, and coordinates operational activities across the Division, including modernization initiatives and organizational restructures. The role involves setting strategic goals, ensuring that operational teams have the resources they need, and establishing performance measures that support continuous improvement. The Director identifies and implements systems and technologies that enhance workflows and allow attorneys and staff to focus on core legal and enforcement work.


As a key member of the Chief's leadership team, the Director works closely with the Deputy Chiefs and Unit Chiefs to ensure that Division priorities move forward cohesively. The Director also helps shape CPD's work culture by promoting employee engagement, supporting training and development, and championing a positive, inclusive, and collaborative environment grounded in equity and innovation. The Director advises the Chief on budgets, public‑facing documents, hiring and personnel matters, organizational changes, and implementation of new policies and procedures. The role requires regular engagement with every unit within the Division and significant interaction with other State agencies, external partners, vendors, and members of the public.


This position offers a meaningful leadership opportunity for someone who thrives in a mission‑driven environment and is energized by complex operations, modernizing systems, and supporting teams that work every day to protect Maryland consumers. The Director of Operations plays a foundational role in ensuring that the Division has the clarity, structure, and momentum it needs to continue delivering high‑impact results for the State of Maryland.

 **Classification:** Admin Prog Mgr III  

  

**Experience:** The ideal candidate brings 8 years of progressively responsible experience in operations, business management, or administrative leadership, preferably within a legal, governmental, or public\-sector environment. They should have demonstrated success managing budgets, optimizing organizational processes, and navigating complex operational challenges. A bachelor's degree is required, and an MBA, MPA, or similar advanced degree is preferred. A JD, MBA, or some experience in the legal profession is also preferred.  

  

**Submission:** Applicants must submit a resume, cover letter, and a list of three professional references, including at least one current or former supervisor. Please note that this job posting will come offline at 6:00 p.m. EST on the closing date.

Lead the Future of Senior Living in Nebraska
  
  

Nye Health Services is seeking an accomplished, strategic, and people\-centered Chief Operating Officer (COO) to help lead one of Nebraska's most respected senior living organizations into its next chapter of growth.
  
  

Reporting directly to the President and serving as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO will provide strategic and operational leadership across multiple service lines, including skilled nursing, assisted living, independent living, rehabilitation, outpatient therapy, memory care, and home health. This executive will play a pivotal role in developing leaders, strengthening operational performance, driving financial success, and ensuring exceptional experiences for residents, families, and team members.
  
  

This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact by leading a mission\-driven organization committed to innovation, operational excellence, and exceptional care.
  
  

About Nye Health Services
  
  

Headquartered in Fremont, Nebraska, Nye Health Services is a family\-owned senior living and healthcare organization serving more than 500 residents across multiple campuses throughout eastern Nebraska. With approximately 750 dedicated team members, Nye provides a full continuum of care, including independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, outpatient therapy, memory care, respite care, and home health services.
  
  

Our mission is to celebrate life by delivering exceptional service and superior value through innovative leadership in personalized care. We believe outstanding resident experiences begin with exceptional team experiences, and we've built a culture where people truly live—and work—happy.
  
  

What You'll Do
  
  

Strategic Leadership
  
  

* Partner with the President and Executive Leadership Team to execute organizational strategy and achieve long\-term goals.
* Lead enterprise\-wide operational initiatives that support growth, innovation, and organizational performance.
* Identify opportunities to improve systems, processes, and operational effectiveness across the organization.


Operational Excellence
  
  

* Provide executive oversight for multi\-site operations across senior living and healthcare services.
* Drive financial performance through census growth, labor optimization, operational efficiency, and fiscal stewardship.
* Ensure regulatory compliance, survey readiness, quality outcomes, and risk management across all service lines.


Leadership Development
  
  

* Coach, mentor, and develop Executive Directors and operational leaders.
* Build high\-performing teams and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Champion Nye's mission, values, and commitment to exceptional service.


What You'll Bring
  
  

* Ten or more years of progressive executive leadership experience in senior living, post\-acute care, healthcare, home health, or another complex multi\-site service organization or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Bachelor's degree required; master’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading large, multi\-site operations with responsibility for financial performance, growth, quality outcomes, and operational excellence.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, labor management, and strategic planning.
* Proven ability to develop leaders, build high\-performing teams, and drive organizational accountability.
* Experience navigating regulatory compliance, quality improvement, and risk management in highly regulated environments.
* Exceptional communication, relationship\-building, and change leadership skills.
* Current Nebraska licensure—or the ability to obtain applicable licensure—is preferred (such as Nursing Home Administrator or Assisted Living Administrator). Clinical licensure is welcomed but not required.

You're an executive who enjoys spending time in operations—not just the boardroom. You know how to translate strategy into measurable results while empowering others to succeed. You build trust quickly, coach leaders through challenges, make thoughtful decisions using data, and create systems that drive sustainable performance. Most importantly, you lead with humility, integrity, accountability, and a genuine passion for serving older adults and the people who care for them.

* Influence the future of a growing, respected healthcare organization.

**RELOCATION ASSISTANCE IS AVAILABLE FOR THIS POSITION.**

**WHO WE ARE**


EPC was conceived and operates to provide anyone who desires to provide for their families through the work they do, an opportunity to do so. Everything we do revolves around the vision of a company that provides safe, quality work, driving customer demand that ultimately results in the creation of new job opportunities in the markets we serve. We focus heavily on our Core Values and expect all our employees to operate with those Core Values in Mind. These Core Values are Live Safe, Customer First, Do the Right Thing, Be at Team Player, and Be Productive.

**WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR**


The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day flow of all aspects of our business and carrying out the vision of the CEO. This position should be a direct reflection of the CEO’s vision and expectations, building and executing a business strategy that aligns with the vision, culture expectations, and growth strategies. This individual will have direct oversight to all functions of the business, including Operations, IT, Human Resources, and Project Management**.**

**WHAT YOU GET TO DO**

* Enforce accountability across all functions within the organization.
* Oversee day\-to\-day business functions and strategy, including human resources, operations, IT, maintenance, safety, and sales.
* Oversee organizational planning, maintenance, and efficiency.
* Prepare and deliver operational reports and management reports.
* Establish KPI reporting and visibility across all departments.
* Identify and execute programs, software, automation, or other levels of optimization to improve organizational efficiencies.
* Ensure compliance on a company, state and federal level.
* Drive sustainable growth and minimize losses.
* Lead outreach and business relations.
* Consistent review of budgets across the organization to ensure alignment.

**WHAT WILL HELP YOU STAND OUT**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Construction, or related field
* MBA or other Master’s degree preferred.
* Diverse business knowledge related to Information Technology, Human Resources, Sales, Safety, and Operations is required.
* Strong analytical skills and strategic thinking abilities.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Superior Project Management skills and experience.
* Ability to lead and motivate cross\-functional teams to achieve project objectives.
* At least 15\+ years’ experience leading a mid\-size company in a high\-level role.
* Prior successful experience in the utilities construction or manufacturing industry is highly preferred.
* Project Management Professional or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification is highly preferred.

**WHAT WE ARE OFFERING**

* Full\-time opportunity in a fast\-growth company!
* Opportunity to work autonomously. None of that micromanaging garbage. We hate that!
* Competitive pay plus incentives.
* Comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision)
* Retirement benefits with company match.
* Company paid time\-off.
* Weekly paychecks!
* Career development and growth opportunities.

**WHAT TO EXPECT**

* This job will be primarily office\-based with exposure to normal office environments and noises.
* This position will require travel based on business initiatives, and locations may be across North America.
* May be required to stand, sit, bend, twist, and reach as part of the job.
* Extended periods of standing on your feet may be required.
* May be required to lift up to 50 pounds.
* Must be able to pass a background check, drug screen, or other job\-related pre\-hire screenings related to the job.

**WHO WE ARE**


EPC was conceived and operates to provide anyone who desires to provide for their families through the work they do, an opportunity to do so. Everything we do revolves around the vision of a company that provides safe, quality work, driving customer demand that ultimately results in the creation of new job opportunities in the markets we serve. The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day flow of all aspects of our business and carrying out the vision of the CEO. * Prepare and deliver operational reports and management reports.

**Chief Operating Officer (COO) – Skilled Nursing Operations**
==============================================================

**Location:** \[OKC, OK]  

**Employment Type:** Full\-Time  

**Reports To:** Ownership / CEO

**About the Opportunity**
-------------------------


We are seeking an experienced, hands\-on **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** to lead the operations of a growing portfolio of **skilled nursing facilities (SNFs)**.


This is a high\-impact leadership position for an experienced skilled nursing operator who understands what it takes to run **high\-quality, financially healthy, well\-managed nursing facilities**.


The ideal candidate may come from a **Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA), Regional Vice President of Operations, Regional Director of Operations, Executive Director, or similar skilled nursing leadership background**.


We are also open to candidates with a **CFO, finance, or healthcare finance background** who have substantial experience with skilled nursing operations and understand how staffing, census, reimbursement, quality, and operational decisions drive facility financial performance.


This is not a purely corporate or administrative role. The COO will be expected to **know what is happening inside each building, understand the numbers, hold leadership accountable, identify problems quickly, and drive measurable improvement.**

**What You'll Own**
-------------------


The COO will have overall responsibility for the operational and financial performance of seven skilled nursing facilities.


Key areas of responsibility include:

* Provide leadership and accountability for all seven facilities.
* Partner with and hold Administrators, DONs, and facility leadership teams accountable for results.
* Establish clear operating standards and consistent expectations across the portfolio.
* Monitor facility performance through regular operational and financial reviews.
* Drive census growth, occupancy, admissions, and referral development.
* Manage labor costs, staffing levels, overtime, agency utilization, and productivity.
* Review facility P\&Ls and identify opportunities to improve revenue, margins, and operating performance.
* Monitor key financial and operational metrics and translate data into action.
* Identify underperforming facilities and develop specific turnaround plans.
* Ensure facilities maintain strong clinical, quality, and regulatory performance.
* Maintain survey readiness and ensure deficiencies are addressed quickly and effectively.
* Monitor rehospitalizations, quality measures, Five\-Star performance, and other key clinical indicators.
* Support recruitment and retention of strong Administrators, DONs, nursing leaders, and other key personnel.
* Develop facility leaders and build a strong management pipeline.
* Work closely with ownership on budgets, forecasts, capital needs, strategic initiatives, and growth opportunities.
* Identify opportunities to improve systems, processes, purchasing, vendor relationships, and overall efficiency.
* Ensure accountability through regular facility visits, meetings, dashboards, and performance reviews.
* Create a culture of ownership, accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------


We are looking for a **builder and operator**, not simply someone who produces reports.


The successful candidate will have a strong understanding of the realities of operating skilled nursing facilities and will be comfortable moving between **operations, people, clinical performance, and financial results**.

### **Preferred Background**


Candidates may come from a variety of backgrounds, including:

* LNHA / Nursing Home Administrator
* Regional Director of Operations
* Regional VP of Operations
* Multi\-Facility SNF Executive
* SNF Executive Director / Administrator
* Healthcare COO
* SNF CFO or healthcare finance executive with significant operational experience
* Senior healthcare operations leader

### **Qualifications**

* Significant experience in skilled nursing, post\-acute care, long\-term care, or a closely related healthcare environment.
* Demonstrated experience managing multiple facilities, departments, or complex healthcare operations.
* Strong understanding of SNF operations, staffing, census, reimbursement, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Strong financial and analytical skills with the ability to understand and manage facility\-level P\&Ls.
* Proven ability to improve operational and financial performance.
* Strong leadership and communication skills.
* Ability to hold senior leaders accountable while developing and supporting them.
* Comfortable using data and KPIs to identify problems and drive decisions.
* Strong problem\-solving and decision\-making skills.
* Willingness to spend meaningful time in the facilities rather than managing exclusively from a corporate office.
* Bachelor's degree preferred; advanced degree or healthcare administration/finance background is a plus.
* LNHA license preferred but **not required for the right candidate**.

**The Person We're Looking For**
--------------------------------


The right person is:

**Hands\-on. Analytical. Accountable. Commercially minded. Operationally strong.**


You should be someone who can walk into a facility, talk with the Administrator and DON, review staffing and census, look at the P\&L, identify the biggest problems, and develop a practical plan to fix them.


You don't have to be the smartest person in every room. You do need to **know how to build strong teams, ask the right questions, recognize problems, and make sure things get done.**

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
**Gemma Services** is a multi\-program nonprofit organization that accompanies more than 3,000 youth and families each year through behavioral health, child welfare, prevention, and special education programs. With three locations across the Greater Philadelphia region, we work every day to ensure that every child and family knows they matter.



Reporting to the Chief Development \& Communications Officer (CDCO), the Director of Development serves as a key member of the Development Department leadership team, responsible for advancing Gemma Services’ fundraising, donor engagement, and community partnership strategies. The Director provides strategic leadership for donor cultivation and stewardship, volunteer and in\-kind giving programs, special events, and external relations initiatives that strengthen awareness of and support for Gemma’s mission. This position manages a portfolio of donors and prospects, develops opportunities for philanthropic growth, and works collaboratively across the organization to build meaningful relationships that generate sustainable resources and deepen community engagement.



Responsibilities include:



* Fundraising \& philanthropic program growth \- Secure philanthropic support for Gemma Services’ mission through the cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and retention of donors and supporters.


* Volunteer Program Leadership \- Develop, implement, and evaluate comprehensive volunteer engagement program with measurable goals that increase community engagement and support for Gemma’s mission.


* Oversee robust in\-kind gifts program \- Lead strategy, growth, and administration of Gemma’s gifts\-in\-kind program to secure items that support Gemma’s programs and special events.


* Special events fundraising \- Along with CDCO, provide strategic leadership for fundraising events, including signature annual Chefs for Gemma benefit and third\-party fundraising initiatives.


* External relations and community partnership \- Strengthen and expand relationships with congregations, businesses, and other external partners to increase awareness of and support for Gemma Services.


* Leadership and department operations \- Assist with the overall management and operation of the Development Department and provide leadership in the absence of the CDCO.



**The position is hybrid; 4 days in\-office in Plymouth Meeting, with 1 day remote depending on time of year, and commuting to other Gemma locations and off\-site meetings in the Philadelphia\-region as needed. Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends for fundraising and volunteer events is required. Must have reliable transportation and be able to travel to Gemma's locations as well as off\-site events as needed.**


**Skill(s):** The Director is a highly organized, relationship\-driven fundraising professional with exceptional interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills and a demonstrated ability to engage, inspire, and steward donors, volunteers, and community partners. This individual brings expertise in donor engagement, volunteer management, special events planning, and donor\-centered fundraising, with a strong commitment to exceptional stewardship and the Association of Fundraising Professionals’ Code of Ethics. Strategic, proactive, and hands\-on, the Director thrives in a fast\-paced environment and approaches opportunities and challenges with a collaborative, solution\-focused mindset, and willingness to roll up their sleeves to achieve results. The Director excels at leading complex projects, managing priorities, and working independently and collaboratively across departments. The Director exercises sound judgment, diplomacy, and discretion; maintains strict confidentiality; and is proficient in leveraging technology and data to advance fundraising goals, including event platforms and donor CRM systems such as Raiser’s Edge.


**A valid driver’s license is required.**


**Experience****:** Five to seven (5\-7\) years or more experience in nonprofit fundraising, with responsibilities including donor relations, direct fundraising, volunteer management, and special event management. Demonstrated experience with donor stewardship, volunteer programs, and relationship management to support advancement of organizational mission.


**Education/Training:** Bachelor’s degree required.

  



Benefits include: 3 health insurance plans, 2 dental plans, educational assistance, a retirement plan with a match, fully paid life, short and long\-term disability, generous PTO, personal holidays, and self\-care activities for our employees.



Join our collaborative team and help Gemma create a world where every person knows they matter.

  

Equal Opportunity Employer  

This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

Posting Information
**Posting Number** PG194876EP
  

**Internal Recruitment** No
  

**Working Title** Assistant Director of Philanthropy, Engineering
  

**Anticipated Hiring Range** Commensurate with education and experience
  

**Work Schedule** Monday \- Friday; 8:00 am \- 5:00 pm, additional hours as needed
  

**Job Location** Raleigh, NC
  

**Department** Engineering Advancement
  

**About the Department**
The NC State Engineering Foundation, Inc. (NCSEF) is a private 501©3 non\-profit organization which raises funds from over 50,000 alumni, friends, industry\-related foundations and other sources to support the College of Engineering at NC State University.  

  

Securing private support is critical to advancing the College in rankings of academic and research universities. More focus is being placed on private endowed support for scholarships, fellowships, and professorships in order to recruit the best students and faculty for our programs. Focus is also being placed on support for capital improvements in order to help offset ongoing significant budget cuts that are being implemented. All of this is necessary in order to have the space and resources available for increased enrollment in engineering.
  

**Wolfpack Perks and Benefits**
As a Pack member, **you belong here,** and can enjoy **exclusive perks** designed to enhance your personal and professional well\-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our **Employee Value Proposition**and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone.  

What we offer:* **Medical**, **Dental**, and **Vision**
* **Flexible Spending Account**
* **Retirement Programs**
* **Disability Plans**
* **Life Insurance**
* **Accident Plan**
* **Paid Time Off and Other Leave Programs**
* **12 Holidays Each Year**
* **Tuition** and **Academic Assistance**
* **And so much more!**

Attain Work\-life balance with our **Childcare** benefits, **Wellness \& Recreation Membership**, and **Wellness Programs** that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community.  

  

*Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part\-Time or Full\-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.*

  

**Essential Job Duties**
The Assistant Director of Philanthropy Engineering is primarily responsible for assisting the College of Engineering Advancement team in identifying and qualifying new major gift prospects for NC State. This role is an excellent entry point for those interested in pursuing a career in frontline major gift fundraising.
  

The Assistant Director will identify and manage a discovery portfolio of alumni and friends with the potential to make $100,000\+ gifts and conduct outreach and meetings (primarily virtual) with these potential prospects. Using a set of criteria and key indicators, they will make a determination of prospects’ readiness to be cultivated toward a major gift within the next 12\-24 months and make referrals to major gift officers. As part of their professional development, the Assistant Director will gain exposure to and in some cases, shadow, the process of advancing these relationships toward the cultivation, solicitation and closure of major gifts in collaboration with the assigned gift officer, as well as make their own Leadership Annual Giving ($1,000\-$99,999\) solicitations.  

**Job Duties:**  

**Discovery and Identification of Prospects:*** Partner with Prospect Development and College of Engineering Advancement team to identify a pool of up to 200 prospective major gift prospects through personal research using tools such as NC State’s alumni/donor database, LinkedIn, and by requesting referrals from colleagues, alumni and friends
* Manage and prioritize a portfolio of discovery prospects. Conduct, document and report on a high volume of personalized, professional outreach by phone, email, social media, video and/or mail to schedule meetings with prospects to achieve goals for outreach attempts, qualifications and meetings
* Write detailed contact reports and send personalized follow\-up communication
* As time allows, conduct projects to identify prospects for and reach out to potential prospects for members of the College of Engineering Advancement team as well as support with stewardship and gift acceptance
  



  

**Meeting and Qualification of Prospects:**
* Meet and qualify alumni and friends by learning more about their “NC State story” – what the university meant to them personally and professionally; express gratitude for prior philanthropic or volunteer support; understand why they choose to give back; and establish how they would like to be involved with the university going forward

**Evergreen, CO 80439 \| Full\-Time \| In Person**

**The Opportunity**

What if fundraising were about more than raising money?

What if it were about helping people find a place in something they care about?

Evergreen Christian Outreach (EChO) is looking for a **Director of Development** who sees fundraising that way.

For more than 35 years, EChO has walked alongside individuals and families in Evergreen and the surrounding mountain communities, helping people move from survival toward greater stability and success. Today, our work includes food access, shelter, client services, housing and utility assistance, employment support, volunteer engagement, ReSale Shop and more.

We are now entering an exciting next chapter.

EChO has an extraordinary history of community support. Individuals, families, businesses, congregations, foundations, volunteers, and community organizations have invested their time, resources, relationships, and generosity in EChO for decades.

**Our opportunity now is to build on that foundation.**

We are seeking a **Director of Development** to lead that effort, to strengthen the systems behind our development work, grow contributed revenue, and, most importantly, deepen EChO’s relationships with the people and organizations who care about our community.

We are looking for someone who understands that people rarely connect with an organization simply because they received a good fundraising appeal.

They connect because something matters to them.

Maybe they have a personal connection to hunger or housing insecurity. Maybe they care deeply about their mountain community. Maybe they want to make a difference for families. Maybe they are looking for a meaningful way to use their resources, relationships, skills, or time.

**Your job will be to listen, discover what matters to people, and help them find meaningful ways to be part of EChO’s work.**

We think of this as building a **community of generosity**.

Generosity can mean a financial gift, but it can also mean volunteering, making an introduction, sharing expertise, advocating for our mission, opening a door, providing resources, or simply standing with EChO and the people we serve.

The Director of Development will help create opportunities for all of those forms of generosity.

· **Build the infrastructure.** Strengthen EChO’s development systems, database, stewardship practices, prospect management, reporting, and use of data.

· **Think strategically about the future.** Build a development program and **team** that can grow with EChO and increasingly engage people beyond the organization’s existing relationships.

This is a role for someone who is comfortable moving between **strategy and relationships, big\-picture thinking and hands\-on execution**.

**Who You’ll Work With**

The Director of Development reports to the Executive Director and works closely with EChO’s Board of Directors, leadership team, staff, volunteers, and community partners.

You will also become a visible and trusted representative of EChO in the community.

This is an opportunity to work alongside people who care deeply about EChO and the people we serve, and to help bring even more people into that community.

new_jobs.description:

That’s why, for two years in a row, our employees have voted Progress a certified Great Place to Work®.

As the demand for professionally managed rental homes continues to grow, so do the opportunities at Progress. We’re looking for passionate professionals who are ready to grow with us, make a difference and be part of something meaningful.

Text “ProgressJobs” to 25000 to chat with Kate, our AI Recruiting Assistant. She can help you explore open roles, apply, and answer your questions in real time.

**Job Summary:**


The Director of Government Relations will represent Progress Residential (“Progress”) by advocating before state and local government officials on policies relevant to Progress Residential, its affiliates, Owners, and Property Managers in the Single\-Family Rental (“SFR”) industry. Reporting to the Vice President of Government Affairs, the Director will be responsible for executing government relations strategies, influencing key decision\-makers, building durable relationships, and effectively communicating Progress’ and/or the industry’s positions before state and local governments, with limited federal engagement as needed.


This role requires a disciplined operator who can manage issues independently while remaining closely aligned with the Vice President of Government Affairs.

* Collaborate closely with internal teams and external consultants to ensure consistent, effective advocacy.
* Establish and maintain strong working relationships with legislators, policymakers, regulators, and government staff.
* Educate and persuade key decision\-makers regarding the SFR industry’s role, concerns, and economic contributions.
* Support efforts to influence the development, modification, and implementation of laws and regulations affecting Progress.
* Advocate for policies that promote fair competition, economic growth, and operational stability.
* Cultivate relationships with industry leaders, member companies, and relevant advocacy organizations.
* Coordinate with other lobbyists and stakeholders to form alliances and coalitions in support of shared policy objectives.
* Represent Progress in industry meetings, conferences, and public forums as directed.
* Prepare senior leadership and market teams for meetings with government officials and regulatory agencies.
* Serve as a reliable surrogate for the Vice President of Government Affairs when appropriate.


Qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in political science, public policy, economics, or a related field preferred (Post\-Graduate degree strongly preferred).
* 7–10 years of experience in government relations, public policy, government service, or a related role; Capitol Hill or state legislative experience required.
* Working knowledge of the single\-family rental industry, housing policy, or regulated real estate sectors.
* Strong understanding of legislative processes, regulatory frameworks, and political dynamics at the state and local levels.
* Proven ability to analyze complex policy issues and translate them into clear advocacy strategies.
* Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
* Demonstrated ability to build, manage, and sustain relationships with policymakers and stakeholders.
* High ethical standards and a demonstrated commitment to compliance with lobbying laws and disclosure requirements.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director oversees media relations, advertising, digital strategy, website management, social media, graphic design, and all external communications.
